I really enjoyed my class with this professor. She was really enthusiastic and was really great at teaching with the small class. This was a discussion class therefore attendance was mandatory. Great energy/teaching style. May be confusion for assignment outlines at times but explains well in person/email.

She was a good prof but the amount of assignments she gave was ridiculous. Her instructions were very unclear and you will ALWAYS have to ask for clarification. Although, the exam was the easiest exam I have taken in university so far. It's an easy A course.

Andrea was a very good french teacher. As a first year student myself she was a bit intimidating to me at first but eventually showed to really care about your understanding of the material. She was also always available outside of class for extra help, and while the course load was heavy, it paid off in the end. Solid choice.

She was a wonderful person, and I thoroughly enjoyed this class. The work load was minimal, but direction for assignments we did have was confusing and unclear. The purpose of the course was to help us understand a content course, but as none of us really struggled with that, the class was rather unfocused. Still, I thoroughly enjoyed this class.
Always encouraging towards the students. Provides good feedback and marks very fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Faulkner is an awesome professor who will try his best to help you succeed if you also put in the effort. If you need extra help make sure you go to him. He is really kind and understanding. He also very helpful. By far one of the best profs I've had so far!

Dr. Faulkner is an incredibly intelligent professor who is very passionate about teaching. He is enthusiastic about what he is teaching and only wants his students to do well, he is a more than fair marker. He will email you if he notices you haven't been to class in a few days. Always makes time outside of office hours to meet. Excellent Prof!
Excellent prof, nothing negative to say.
Cool guy. He makes the material easy.

A really good prof. A little boring, but very clear, and very helpful. You can tell he really knows what he's talking about. Goes a little fast at times, but makes it VERY EASY to get a really good mark.

I LOVE prof. Faulkner. He's an amazing teacher, keeping the class interested and he definitely knows what he's talking about. I would take his class again any day. Course has a lot of reading but definitely worth it. He's not the type of prof. to trick you on exams, he's extremely fair. Great guy! Take his class!!
Dr. Faulkner is an incredible Professor. He professes very well and is always there when someone needs help. Our class has to go to WLU next term for GRK 202W and we're all going to miss his class!

The best prof I have had so far. So, so helpful and wants you to do well. He even arranged study sessions - with his free time - outside of term so that you can keep up in your Greek. If you have a chance to have him as a prof, I highly recommend him.
Dr. Faulkner is AMAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAZING. Enough said :).

A great fellow! I enjoyed every one of his classes. He made sure to arrange a meeting with me when I was struggling in some portions of Greek. He's a very dedicated teacher, and has a great sense of humour!

One of my favorite Profs. Very knowlegeable, and excellent at teaching. Very flexible office hours, and always willing to help out a student who needs it. He clearly loves his job and it shows in his teaching. I would recomend any class that he taught.
Very smart prof. Has some good stories

I absolutely loved this professor - learned a ton, but you have to do the work.  I would highly suggest taking any class by him - he gives a lot of easy marks so put the effort in to make up for the tests you may or may not do well on.  If you study/participate/do assignments - you should do awesome

Faulkner was passionate about Mythology and tried to keep his students interests, which he did. He was a pretty good professor! However, it would have been better if he posted the notes prior to class and made them a bit more useful. Otherwise, he was very good!

Great Prof. who is very helpful. Easy to approach and has flexible office hours to meet your needs. Quiet, but concise. Uses Athenaze every class. Do the assigned homework or you will fall behind and get lost. 5 in class tests, participation/attendance in labs (15%) , mid-term, and cummulative exam (30% of final mark).
CWC was my favorite class because of Professor Russel. He truly wants students to succeed and will tell you what to study for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Russell is such a good guy. I've had him for the past three semesters (including interim) for humanities and he genuinely cares about his students beyond just their grade in his class. He's helpful and gives great feedback on papers, and emailing him is a breeze. I've loved being in his class, and would gladly take more classes with him.

Professor Russell is a chill dude. He is very understandable if you have tough things going on (family emergencies, etc) and need extensions. He was my favorite Professor my first semester. I highly recommend taking his class. His lectures/seminars are really interesting and laidback. He has a lot of books we read and writing assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I have always struggled with math, let alone statistics, but Mr. Wright made math much easier to understand. He responded back in a reasonable manner, and was always willing to help if you did not understand the material. Would definitely recommend!
I loved having Mr. Wright he made stats understandable and was very nice. He would even meet after class with students who needed more support! He was the best!

I took professor Wright for a hybrid elementary statistics course and I would recommend him to anyone and everyone. His notes are very clear and he will make sure you understand the material. If you are having trouble with the material he will help you.

Mr. Wright is the ONLY reason I passed Statistics. He was amazing. If you need help, just stay after class or shoot him an e-mail. He is very willing to help. He also gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. I recommend him to everyone!

Stats are hard for most but Mr. Wright will help and is easy to talk with. He responds to all emails in a timely manner. He is all business in the class room but can crack a joke every once in a while. If you struggle with any math, I highly recommend Mr. Wright. Remember to email him or go by his office. He welcomes students questions.
The subject was really hard! He gives extra credit and is willing to help if you just ask!!!

Mr. Wright is an awesome math teacher! I took his statistics class during the summer semester and he was very helpful. I don't consider myself to be very good at math and I got an A in the class. Make sure you come to class on time and stay on top of you work and you should do fine! He wants his students to succeed and he gives extra credit!
Mr. Wright is a good teacher. Just be prepared to take the class seriously and STUDY..you also might want to get tutoring help. If you let him know you care he will help you out.

Andrew Wright is the best math professor! Take him! He is patient, laid back, and straight forward. He gives lots of extra credit. Prior to exams you will have an overview day. He is in his office when he says also in tutoring lab. Homework is not bad if you stay on top of it.

He is a very helpful teacher. ewill always answer a question when you have one. Has plenty of examples for understanding. Attendance not ALWAYS mandatory, but he'll let you know. Test's are pretty easy, just be sure to do your homework online.
Mr. Wright is a very patient teacher and very helpful. He takes time to help you when you have problems.
He's adorable with his North Carolina accent.  He's well prepared and always willing to help.  I wish all teachers were like him.  :)
Mr Wright IS THE BOMB! I was part of his first Stats teaching and loved the class. I would definitely recommend him :)
This professor is laid back. He works with you on homework and other class room work. He is funny. If you a have never had this subject before he wolud  be a good teacher
He is hands-down the best math teacher I have ever had.  If you're not a math person but need this class for your major (like myself), definitely take Mr. Wright.  You won't be sorry!
Is so smart about what he teaches!

Once he got the hang of teaching (1st year teacher) he did everything fine. Caters to the students' requests and needs. Tests are difficult but not impossible if you study hard. He gives extra credit and grades fairly. I recommend him.

Dr. Long, is by far the best english professor at Lakeland! I took her class in 2012. Her course is not the easiest, but it's college! She's very helpful and very knowledgeable. She is fair and stern in grading, her notes directs you on how to become a better writer! I highly recommend her class.
i loved dr long!! i really wish she would teach the next english class. At the end of the semester I had a 89.3% and she even rounded it up!! i would highly recommend

This woman is completely unreasonable. Issues are black/white. A lot of work for very little knowledge gained. I earned a B but hated her teaching style (she is very,very moody) Typical "I'm way better than you" Phd attitude. Easily summed up by the simple saying "C U Next Tuesday".

I took a total of 3 classes with her and would take more if I needed to. I learned alot from her and think she is a great teacher. It's true there is A LOT of reading, and the discussion boards where time consuming, but just turn off the TV and open your books people. You don't have to be brillant, just do the work.

Michelle Long was one my first teachers I had when I started college and she sparked a fire of learning in me and I really apperciated it!! Some people did not like her but those were also ones who didn't show up for class or showed up late. She was always available when I needed help or just a little extra encouragement!!!

Horrible class, I did online, big mistake. She would be-little you, as if she is way better than you.  Took summer class, and did on average 8 essays per week!  Not a good teacher at all.  I worked my tail off and got a b. put on average 27 hours per week into class! would not recommend at all!

Probably one of the worst professors I have had at Lakeland. This professor cannot be reasoned with. Her assignments are pointless and unnecessarily difficult to understand and complete. I would not recommend her to anyone. Horrible experience!
As the other posts pointed out, she has lots of mood swings, but her class is indeed easy, but not a good teacher. She has little care in student performance, and much more care in herself.

This was an online class.  She was pretty cool.  She had her little mood swings now and again.  She was always very quick to reply to email.  I gues I enjoyed the class, but I do love english, so...I recommend her class because the grading is pretty easy.  Make sure you CLEARLY read and understand the instructions.
Took online English Comp. 1110.  Tough grader, but overall not too bad.  Take only if you are willing to put in the extra effort an online course requires.

Great teacher. She is hard, but is you put effort in, you get alot out. Tests are essay, plus a term paper. The content was slighly boring, but she is a fun teacher and is excited about what she teaches. Alot of reading is involved, along with weekly quizzes (so you actually have to read to do well). I would reccomend her for serious students.
I took this class online and she was very helpful.  If you are thinking about taking this online, I would highly recommend it.  It is fairly easy, but you still have a lot of work to do.

She's THE sweetest teacher I ever had. Super caring.. Maybe she changed the way  she graded bc in this class there wasn't no paper exams or quizzes..Just a bunch of work you had to do..for the midterm you just had to do a presentation online with the prof only for 10 min max. A final paper work and a group presentation.. She's  amazing..Love her!!

She's a sweetheart, she means well but her exams are way too hard. We also had a paper to do which was impossible to complete I'm pretty sure everyone had a bad grade. Also READ THE BOOK AND TAKE NOTES!!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: her exams are SO hard but she cares a lot about her students and wants them to pass so she's always changing our gardes, it's great but I wish she could make her exams easier so we wouldn't have to email her after every test

It was her first time teaching a course, so after the midterm mishap, we definitely curved our grades and made the final easier. Grade boosters include the 3 mini papers you need to write; very easy. She also bribes the students to participate with chocolate haha!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Très bon prof, se soucie beaucoup de ses élèves, utilise des techniques d'enseignement originales. Prenez son cours de droit de l'environnement si vous en avez la chance!L'une des meilleures pédagogues de l'UQAM.
No Comments

C'est la meilleure prof qu'on peut avoir!!! elle explique super bien, est passionnée par sa matière, vraiment la prof à avoir quand tu commences ton bac en droit!! En plus, on peut la tutoyer et pas obligé de l'appeler Maître, juste Annie c'est correct!
If you can't handle Daimsis, you can't handle the practice of law. He's tough but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I second all the other reviews here, he is a MUST take if you have the chance. He won't be here for long (max 1-2 more years) so prioritize getting into his classes if you can. Does not use slides so make sure to pay attention in class. Miss class, you wont pass.

One of the greatest professors in the Faculty. Prof Daimsis has a deep understanding of the materials. He doesn't just teach you the black-letter law, but really gives you the rational behind the case law. Should really pay attention to what he said in the lectures.

Professor Daimsis is the greatest professor at the University, that's it, that's the list. He is VERY well respected around the world in arbitration, he is Canada's expert. His upper year courses are now by application so that he isn't tied to the bell curve, and it works! He wants to give out A's, and he will do it if you let him.
His lectures are fun and his exam questions are straightforward if you pay attention in class and read them properly. Unlike some other profs in law school, his exams are easy to finish.

I honestly do not understand where those bad comments are coming from. You can not have a better professor than Daimsis in your entire law school. He knows the material and he is an amazing lecturer who uses the Socratic method. Those who say that he is arrogant, they defiantly can not distinguish arrogance from self-confidence.
Best prof you can encounter in law school. knows his job very well. his lectures are fun and transformative. Did not miss a lecture.

uOttawa better be paying this man. He's a treasure. Not easy, but fair. His lectures are top-tier. Looked forward to every class. My advice: do the readings and make your own briefs, then supplement them with the in-class material. 

PS. Read exams carefully. The devil is in the details.

He is the worst prof I have ever had. He is rude, condescending, inappropriate and demeaning. He doesn't respect class time and thinks he is better than everyone. He acts like he knows better than all the courts. He needs a wake up call on respect. On exams, he will frequently give out 0s on questions even though you got most of the elements.
Good prof who may be perceived improperly by people. He cares but is extremely busy but is honest, direct and wants you to be better.

Professor Daimsis is an amazing professor. He knows his stuff. He's tough, critical and doesn't pull punches. Not because he's mean-spirited but because he cares and wants you to improve. That became really obvious when I mooted with him. It's any student's honour to be coached and mentored by him if you can handle it.

Brilliant prof who knows his stuff and genuinely cares about students' success. His lecturing style is super clear and compelling; he's a great speaker and has no trouble holding the class's attention. The subject matter (international arbitration) was really interesting, especially taught from his expert perspective. Highly recommend.
Best teacher I've had in my whole law school career!

He is one of the best professors at UoO, at least that I've had. His lectures are extremely engaging, you barely have to take down any notes because he conveys the material so well and in such a manner that just makes sense. Hilarious too. Overall, excellent. I would not hesitate to take him again. You will learn tons in this class.

Prof Daimsis is by far the best professor. He believes in his students' competence and refuses to spoon-feed case ratios. His exams are extremely fair! Yes, he has high expectations during lectures for students to come prepared and understand the cases, but his exams are solely based on information discussed, and aren't filled with trick-questions
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: A prof unafraid to poke fun at the ever-so-slightly non-PC material. What a breath of fresh air. Course is engaging and he encourages participation. Muster up the courage to ask/answer questions in class, and I guarantee you'll walk away with solid understanding of contracts. Really knows his stuff, and will actually help if you ask in office hrs.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Good prof. Laid back and funny. Mandatory 1L class (content/PPTs set by the school?), so the material wasn't the most exciting, but he does a great job sifting through the important/not-so-important info. Teases students but isn't mean... ADR will be fun if you keep this in mind & participate.

He's been described as a "moot god" at school before, hence "respected" in my tags. He's funny, he gets through the material, and does indeed give off that "sleezy lawyer" vibe. That said, he cares about teaching students how to be lawyers rather than simply teaching student the law. If you can get him for ADR, I recommend him.

Great guy but not a great prof, hes lectures are a tad boring and detailed but then again there are very few classes he shows up for. The class itself is interactive with lots of opportunities for engaging questions and debate. Lively class overall and generally nice guy who also happens to be the moot coach for the law school.

Big fish in a little pond syndrome. Brags a lot to elicit the admiration of students. Arrogant demeanor. Phones it in during most lectures (probably bc he's bored with material he knows well, and it's all about him, not about your learning). Superficial charm - has that sleazy lawyer vibe. But you will learn some useful techniques.

This class is challenging but rewarding. This class will prepare you for the "real world" and is a must-take if you are prepared to put the work into it. I was also better prepared for my contracts exam because he compares and contrasts  international contracts with the common law. He will make you think outside of the box.

Listen 0Ls, if you take his thematic class be ready for an intense wrap up to the course in terms of workload (for a 1L thematic course anyway), but Daimsis is hands-down the best prof I had this year. If you're interested in the subject, you won't regret it.
You probably wont get an A, but you have to be really dumb and not pay attention at all to get lower than a B.  Just listen to what he says in class and do his practice exams and youll do fine.

Daimsis is an excellent professor.  Those complaining about him are just poor law students who do not know how to write an exam. He expects clarity in writing and well thought out answers. If you're a crappy writer and do not understand legal precedents, his class is not for you. One of the best uOttawa has. Heads up the Moots for a REASON.

If you’re an extremely gifted student this professor is for you however, if you are not stay as far away as you possibly can from this showboat. Oh he’ll entertain you BUT WITH his final I guarantee that any laughter will come to a screeching halt when you see what he serves up to you. Use to A's & B's, welcome to your 1st C or worse!

Great prof, funny, knows is his stuff about international trade law and UNCITRAL.  One of the most engaging classes I've had at law school.  U of o is lucky to have this prof... let's hope the school doesn't screw up and lose him to the private sector.

Not as impressed as some other posters. I wasn't taken by his superficial charm and found that he was incredibly condescending; he quickly skimmed over cases including some very tricky concepts. Contrary to what he says, he does try to trick you in his NP contracts exam which is 2 hours but should be 3. Doesn't always respond to emails....
Prof with benefits ;)

Hard maker no doubt but fair.  If you show interest and demonstrate that you are trying he will help you to achieve the success you're working towards.  Was awarded capital educator's award for 2011 and by no accident.  I entered contracts law dreading it and walked out loving contracts.  Must take class.  He will teach you the law correctly.
Amazing prof! Very enthusiastic and passionate. Makes you work hard and think for yourself. Can be arrogant and sarcastic, but is still overall entertaining and makes you want to succeed!

Should not be teaching first year contracts. Displayed palpable disregard for the students in his class. Does not hold regular office hours. Canceled classes. Skipped over readings. Did not review course material prior to exams. Marking was arbitrary. Avoid.

Good first year contracts prof, will force you to think mroe like a lawyer and work things out on your own. He is friendly, but some find him intimidating. However, he slacks off in 2nd term to focus on his moot teams. He is a fair marker (although consistency is questionable) but he will try to trip you up on the exam, and then deny it.

Great guy to have as a first year prof. Teaches the law and gives you the tools you need to think for yourself - but he doesn't make it easy. You have to work for it, which in the long run is a good thing. Also, if you say stupid things in class he will call you out on it, so think before you talk.
he is an amasing prof
Doesn't return emails.
No Comments

had him in 2007-2008 for 1st year contracts - very simple lectures, not much controversy/theory/critical thinking at all. he wants you to know the facts very practically. efficency, not creativity, is the name of the game on the exam. outside of class, he offers more depth than you'll get from the somewhat superficial lectuers. points for clarity.

Really nice guy. Funny, sarcastic and really knows his contracts and business law. Cares about students doing well but getting there fairly. Not your typical prof and will make you think about the bigger world view. Don't take him if you are not prepared to think as you're writing your exam. Read questions and facts carefully!!!

Very well-structured class with assignments that genuinely helped me improve drawing & animation skills! He's also a kind and patient prof. The Maya 3D assignments will require lots of time to complete, so definitely start those early. My classmates and I thought that grading was pretty harsh though (esp compared to other profs).
Grades fairly and explains well.

Dr. Lei is the linear algebra prof at UOttawa this year; I LOVE LOVE LOVED his class. His lectures are clear and to the point, and his grading criteria is very fair! Read the textbook's recommended readings, attend the lectures, do the recommended exercises and practices, put in the work, and you will get an A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Fantastic linear algebra prof, highly recommend!

Awesome guy, great notes, hard course. You need to do a lot of practice questions if you want to do well. His English isn't that good, but he knows it and really tries hard to make you understand. Stops at the end of each topic to allow people to ask questions. Quizzes with him are very difficult and only out of 4 marks (1 per question).

Cutest prof EVER!! He is so funny, whether he is trying to be or not. He is very approachable in person, and immediately responds to questions you send by e-mail. He is also very considerate, e.g. he drops lowest quiz grade and takes the class' opinion on quiz scheduling and such. If you are able to get him as a prof, do not hesitate!

The final was ok but the quizzes are where I struggled but he is very accommodating as it relates to quiz marks, like he dropped our lowest quiz mark. Overall I've had worse professors so he's actually one of mcgill's better math profs.
Best math prof at mcgill. Very funny and gives good lecture notes.
Eager to help, enthusiastic, good examples and suggested textbook questions.
Lei is very clear and funny. He is eager to help and lets you ask questions in class. Talks/writes very fast but writes good lecture notes. Overall very hard course but Lei is a very good prof.
Prof Lei is a good prof as far as math profs go at McGill. I would strongly recommend him because he is eager about teaching and about being understood. Very cute prof.
Pretty clear and funny, but overall a difficult course.

Coursework: You have 3 assignments in the whole semester+ the final exam is a take home!
She is super approachable, respectful of your french level, is a fair and kind grader. I would take her class again! Most of the classes are fun and engaging as well. 
We also had a pot luck in our last class!
She was nice and caring that wants students to succeed. Her exams were very easy.
Very smart and friendly professor. No tricky questions on the exam. If you attend all the lectures, you get an A+

Arezu is a very smart Prof. makes sure students participate in each lecture. Makes learning fun. Shows a lot of movies of what is really going on inside the cells.  She is very fair. I really miss that class.

Very smart prof and she knows a lot about anatomy, however she is sometimes difficult to follow and sometimes refused to answer questions due to time contraints which made it difficult to grasp some concepts.
Rough English... hard to follow.  Smart woman though!
No Comments
No Comments

Grading criteria was clear, grades were fair. Ariel kept the lectures engaging and interesting, the lectures did not feel repetitive, I feel as though I've taken a lot away from the class. Would highly recommend.
Ariel is an amazing lecturer. Really knows how to captivate students. Loves group work!
Amazing lecturer. Really knows how to captivate students. Loves group work!

I definitely recommend going to lectures! The slides won't have a lot of info and the readings can be tough, but he does a great job explaining and giving examples for abstract concepts. Really interesting lectures, and I loved that assignments seemed designed to get you to think about and engage with content, instead of just trying to quiz you.
I've had Ariel twice now. I've enjoyed both classes I took with him.

Highly recommend, very interactive. You will get a good mark if you put in the work. This class was definitely not boring and was easy on marks as 30% is simply for participating in weekly discussion. The content of the course is interesting and he is overall a very nice and helpful professor. If you don't try and keep up you will obviously do bad.
Final paper is a joke 12-14 pages... no topics given, no expectations, no help.

Amazing professor, studies in addictions was my favourite class and he was the one of the best prof's I had! Very clear of what is expected within the course and make the material interesting and easy to understand.

Ariel was the best prof I had in university. His lectures are so engaging and hes so full of knowledge he doesnt rely on slides or textbooks. His essay topics are so open you really get the chance to research something youre interested in. Tip: Do an actual critical analysis and apply theories for papers - A+ students get Cs for not getting this
first class with him. hes soooooooo passionate about his class and si without a doubt kinda and energetic

Where do I begin? Genuinely cares about his students success. He is an amazing teacher & he make the class interesting and fun. HIGHLY recommend Ariel for SOCI 3055. My favourite teacher so far at Carleton. The content is interesting, his assignments/midterm are awesome. No complaints at all. Take a class with him!!

Ariel was very passionate about what he was talking about and took the basic sociological concepts and turned them into more philosophical. He makes you think deeper and outside the box. You need to take good notes, his slides aren't the best. His exam was tough, but if you asked questions and studied, you'll do fine. His paper was tough too!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer! Lecture's very insightful, engaging and informative. Doesn't put up written slides be prepared to take notes. Always available to help. Very fair in grading. His midterms are a little challenging so study well for those , make sure to especially keep up with the readings and take notes if you want a good grade on the midterm.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Best prof I've had in my 4 years. Expects students to engage in the course + the material but doesn't give assignments that are too hard. Good at synthesizing complex material. Students always want to chat with him & he takes time to do this. The last few classes weren't worth grades but almost everybody showed up anyway which speaks for itself.
Good professor but for a class that many take as a joke it was overly tough (marking wise). Go to class and pretend you care and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Im currently taking this class.  He is the best professor I've had at Carleton thus far.  His lectures and his delivery are engaging and everyone that I know in the class completely agrees.  His development of every topic is deep and he has a great understanding of everything he teaches.  He also allows for a lot of commentary from the students.

Awesome professor to have! Ariel really cares about his students. This was a fairly average course. If you show up to class and pay attention you will do well on the exams and the papers are generally graded pretty fairly - just watch grammar as he is a stickler for it. Great lectures as he is dynamic and engaging in class.

Great teacher. Dr. Fuenzalida is very well educated in the topic of social theories and has a great explanation to help students understand as well. He takes time to thoroughly explain the important social theories of classical theorists as well as post modern ones. There is mandatory reading and it is very important to do the online work.

The lecture material could be interesting, but his delivery lacks. He expects students to post online around 50 times during the semester (as an approximation). Your mark for online postings is graded by how many other people post, so if you don't think you can spare the extra hours, you will miss 10% of your grade.

1 Midterm, 3 short assignments, 1 final. All long answers. Exams are based solely on textbook, so definitely make sure to study it thoroughly. He was very clear on what we had to know, very helpful, nice, fair guy, and can talk to him about anything.  Lectures are awesome course requires work but I would definitely recommend this prof!
Honestly, I studied harder for this class than any other class, and I did horribly. Not sure if it was him or the TA's, but he is a HARD MARKER. I thoroughly regret taking this class.

Very helpful professor with sound presentation skills. Written assignments were fair and definitely helped my mark. We were tested solely on textbook material which was a challenge at time, in that the lecture material was not always relevant material to study. Focused a lot on specific aspects (verbatim) out of textbook on exam.

Such a great prof. If you are ever struggling with anything, go see him in office hours, he is SO helpful, clear and supportive of your ideas and writing. The class can be a bit dry but he's a great lecturer and very passionate. If you put the mark in, you can do really really well in his classes!

Also, the prof who engages students by using videos. Very helpful at office hours. My experience was that most policy students *loved* the course and found it to be a fun and easy bird-course. Most of the SOCI students complained about the 3-hour length and weren't very engaged to begin with. Bottom-line: you get what you put in.

Best prof at Carleton. Seems dry at first, but he offers the most mind-shattering analysis of addiction. He truly wants his students to learn and grow. Offers a radically different understanding of addictions and drugs. Long lectures, but easy exams and essay. Readings are optional.

He's extremely intelligent & if u pay attention u will learn a lot. His exam questions are long and require a lot of time & preparation, but he points out exactly where in the readings to look. He's very willing to help u format  ur essay answers to ensure the best answer possible. Also he provided me with a lot of research material for the essay.

Assigns an insane amount of reading that is never tested on or discussed in class. Tells you exactly what you need to have read for the exams, making the rest of your reading completely useless(which is annoying after you've read it all). I found his lectures very boring and impossible to follow, couldn't listen for more than an hour.

If you want to read for the next 15 years then take this class. The course material is interesting but for the most part everything is made far more complicated than needed. He knows what he is talking about, but the the amount of readings in this course are ridiculous, and I am quite familiar with heavy-reading courses.
Awesome - excellent critical analysis of 'addiction'.  Very abstract - very much into his work.
I loved Ashley as a teacher. She knows how to break the movements down so everyone can understand. She's funny and entertaining but knows her stuff. Take from her if you can:)
Amazing dance teacher. Took me from not being able to move my feet to any rhythm to being a halfway decent dancer. Definitely the hottest dance teacher as well.

Ashley is just out of this world.  She would twirl and spin and I would just get dizzy!  Man, did I learn to dance like a tiger because of her.  Thank you for the amazing lessons, I shall not forget thee.

I was so nervous when I signed up for this class because dancing just isn't my thing. However, Ashley changed that. Not only is Ashley a talented dancer (HUGE understatement), she is also a phenomenal teacher. Even if you lack the talent, Ashley creates a fun atmosphere that drives each student to excel. She's also gorgeous. Highly recommended!

Ashley is so fun to work with. This class is easy if you love to dance. I think, like most dance classes, all professors are very strict with grading technique. But the class is fun and a good way to meet new people! I totally recommend Ashley!

She is a tough grader but does a good job at explaining things, so if you know the parts of a case analysis and understand everything, you'll be fine. She's really nice and always gives feedback when you ask. She's always answering questions in office hours. She never takes the whole class time. There is a lot of in class group work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is a nice professor. Lectures are short, but they do explain how to do Case Analysis'. It is an easy class to pass as long as you understand how to write a case analysis'. She is unclear when she grades. If you know how to write one case analysis, you can write any case analysis on any topic. If writing is hard, I do not recommend taking her.

I remember being really afraid to take Professor Khan's class, but she is not as bad as it seems. She is nice and caring. Study how to write a case analysis' beforehand to do well. Make sure that you read and understand all of the required material before case analysis exams. It helps! All she wants to see if that you put effort into your work.

Took her for fall 2019 the class was once a week. She would take the entire class time, tough grader but the work is doable, requires critical thinking but a stress free class. The reviews scared me since she replaced a professor i actually chose. I ended up staying but she is very boring. Although as long as you try your best writing you'll be ok.

Professor Khan is not as bad as everyone is making it seem. She really cares about the subject and gives everyone a fair chance to stay on track. Homework is easy and must do it to be successful in the class. Her grading on exams (case analysis's) is questionable at times but do all the work and at least do decent on her tests and you will be fine.

Professor Khan doesn't deserve the 1.0 ratings below. I took her reluctantly after having read those reviews. Although her grading is a bit random, a B is very doable. She is very nice and cares about the class. She rarely uses up the entire class time lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Pros: Always ready to answer your questions. 3 attempts Mindtap homework and highest grade. Teaches you how to write with business etiquette. Cons: Reads off slides which tends to make class boring. Strict grading of writing assignments. Advice: Actually read the book. Just speeding through hw and winging the writing assignments is not good enough
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Shes a very nice professor whos always on time, but reads directly off slides. In-class writings happen very often and grading isnt consistent. You use the online textbook a lot and have constant online homework but theyre easy points! Not too bad.

Vague grading. Arbitrarily takes off points from papers without good explanations. Reads off the slides. Makes you turn in a rough draft but doesn't give feedback??? In-class writings count for 30% of grade but there's no practice writings. You're expected to just read and then automatically know how to write a perfect essay in class.

Professor Khan is not bad she is an okay professor. We have one writing assignment in class every week and she is a tough grader but if you always go to class participate and do your work its an easy B. She has 4 quizes and hw assignments are due weekly online. She DOES TAKE ATTENDANCE. She also does read of the powerpoints.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: All she does is read off the slides which is literally word for word from the textbook. Like HELLO I know how to read... She does not explain anything. In-class writings happen almost every week and the grading never makes sense. There is homework due before every class. It's online and the textbook is online. Attendance is taken class.
I guess it was an okay class but I didn't feel very engaged. Also asks for weekly comments on the reading to be handed in in person.

Overall, she is a good teacher. She is passionate about the material and seems enthusiastic to teach. Her lectures were perhaps too long sometimes, but that's because she tried to make sure the students understood the material.

Amazing teacher! Her grading criteria are fair and easy to understand she is also a very quick responder for emails. Super knowledgable and lectures are interesting.  She is francophone so she has a bit of an accent. She was so nice, the final was a take home which I really appreciated. If you get a chance take her!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good prof. The class is well structured. Her lectures are clear. She gives lots of readings but they won't totally affect your grade. Only 3 papers/semester, no pop quizzes. not a hard grader but you definitely have to do the work right to get a good grade. Would take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: her accent is really strong and her microphone sucks its hard to focus. also she just speaks generally/theoritically, her powerpoints are not clear to follow and have lots of typos (so do the TAs, also francophone). its been 6 six weeks and she hasnt mentioned a single case study, its all theory but i can barely understand what shes saying
She's super nice! Go to class for the notes (or don't, but definitely keep up). Lots of problems to do but they weren't technically difficult. Exam was what was reviewed in class.

Lectures are very informative and cover many practice problems. She clearly states every subject on each test beforehand and gives a lot of suggested practice problems. Lectures and tutorials are optional, all course material can be done individually on the textbook. Great professor and class, is not too hard if you pay attention and PRACTICE A LOT

The entire class is going over example problems, and the tests are problems nearly identical to those in class.  Excellent teacher, and very knowledgeable.  The course is exam-heavy, and the exam was noticeably harder than the tests and practice exams she posts, but that is my only point of complaint.  You're lucky if you get her for math 1005.

this prof is amazing, she gives thorough explanations and breaks down complicated questions to a very basic level, she is the best math teacher ive had. for this class all you need to do is pay attention to her lectures and brush up on some concepts and you should be fine.

She cares about her students and her lectures are great. She clearly indicates what will be found on the tests so it's easy to do well. 

Just attend the lectures, do the tutorials and the suggested homework and a A+ is almost guaranteed. 

Has a strict rule against talking in her lectures, which is appreciated.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. She is very friendly. Example-loaded lectures which is great. Tests are very fair and accurately cover the material taught. Do every suggested exercise, and the tutorials on your own, and you will get an A+. Great reintroduction to math as a mature student. Would take again, and hopefully I do.

Clear explanations and seems to actually care about our understanding of the content. If you go to the lectures and do the textbook questions you'll be fine. Has a strict rule against talking in her lectures which is nice
Helpful Professor

She's a great professor and conducts great lectures. Answers questions and emails well, and makes sure everyone understands. She does show up to class late sometimes though, and sometimes she moves through problems a little too fast. But overall, she was great, would totally take her again.

Amazing prof. Clear course outline, has previous lectures recorded, detailed notes (with solutions), and provides so many examples in the lectures. I like the way she writes down the exercises on paper and explains them throughout, really useful when learning 1005. The tests were easy (in my opinion) and the final was decent too. She is the GOAT.

Amazing prof. Explains everything in detail and doesn't go into nonsense that won't help you solve problems. She answers any questions and will do her best to help you understand. Class was divided into 4 tests and a final exam. Tests were easy, just study for them and you'll get A+ in the class. Class was also easy and she is very nice.

She explains the concept and then solves many examples, covers basic algebra steps, and writes on paper. Examples during lectures are enough. Her tests are straightforward. She posts the test and tutorial answers and questions. She posts her solved notes, online videos from previous semesters, suggested problems, and sample finals.

Interesting content and great professor. Expectations were clear. You had to show up to do well on the exams because there were more in depth explanations in class. 3 midterms, a final and a lab. The lab was straightforward and provided application of the concepts covered in class.

Amazing prof! I hope she teaches more courses in the future. Super straightforward about expectations, tests are clear, leaves time during lectures for questions/discussions. Lots of assessments and a hands on lab so lots of room for improvement/feedback throughout the course! Thank you Dr. Toor!
Dr. Schneider is a little rough and some may be offended by his language and joking nature. If you are sensitive and do not have thick skin, don't take a course with him.

I don't know if he's great teaching other classes but for Case Conceptualization he is horrible, not clear and doesn't teach well. He expects at least 4 students to drop his class. He did not provide one complete example about the way we were supposed to analyze a case. Everyone was freaking out about the exam. Four people dropped. Do NOT take him!
Great profs, one of the best. Funny and fair.
great teacher, does not curse enough for me.  Is extremely funny. Nice, genuine, real.
Overall, good teacher. funny (sometimes), curses too much.

Very knowledgeable prof. He explained each lecture with great detail and added things that weren't on the slides so it is important to show up. Labs are very straightforward and the field outing we had was lots of fun (lafleche caves). The midterm was very straightforward and had no surprises.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: 2 projects, midterm, and final. The TA's randomly took off marks off the projects as if they didn't even read them. If it wasn't for the online exams, half of us would've failed. Midterm was very fair, final was insane: mc qs with PARAGRAPHS for answers. We barely had enough time. He tells you which slides to study though, sweet prof

Overall professor leclerc makes the exams very straightforward but the papers were confusing. Course content was focused on child development/psychology and didnt really link back to origins of disease until the last lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Straightforward, makes pharmacology concepts easy to understand, and gives hints as to what is on the exams!

Super straight forward lectures, uses MS teams and answers all questions outside of class time, midterm and final were easy if you study the slides. He tells you exactly what you need to know! Very caring.
Great guy

Benoit makes a hard course like pharmacology as easy and straightforward as possible. The two written assignments are very helpful to study off of and you do learn a lot from them. The exam questions were straight from his powerpoint slides so as long as you put in the work and study you will do great in this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He should not be teaching the English section. It is extremely hard to understand him, and most students had to teach themselves the course material. All of the examination questions are based on the slides however the number of questions he gives you is almost triple the number of other classes with no extra time. Avoid him to do well.

Hes not a bad prof but definitely shouldnt be teaching the english stream. His online classes this year consisted of him narrating his slides in a very confusing manner. I would suggest choosing a different prof for this class. The midterms and exams were fair but require a lot of self teaching.

Everyone puts down Prof Leclerc but he's honestly a rlly good choice!! Assignments for all profs are the same, can be done in groups and pretty easy. He tells u which slides to study so exams are easy to do well. He gives hints sometimes in class but lectures are tempting to skip. Pharm isnt that interesting, lots of memorizing but hes not petty

Although Prof Leclerc was slightly hard to understand because of his heavy accent, his midterm and final were fair. Just make sure to listen in lectures (which you will fall asleep in) and keep up with the course material as it is difficult. The paper isn't too hard, but don't leave it till last minute as it takes a lot of time to do.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes really an amazing prof! Hes super helpful to his students and lectures arent mandatory to attend, but he gives hints for the exams and specifies what you should know for the exams (really helpful for a heavy course like pharmacology)! If you go to his office hours hes always willing to give you study tips and feedback, and hes caring!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great to have a prof who can answer my questions. He is friendly and try to help me out. The course is heavy, but I have learned a lot more than other courses!

He should not be teaching an English course, his English is so poor. The lectures are pointless to attend due to him just reading off the slides. You need to memorize everything and know every little detail because he will ask you about every little thing on the exams
He cannot speak English and he was teaching an English Microbiology and Immunology course... His tests were hard and did not match up with what was taught in class.

He should not be teaching an english class; his english is terrible. He reads directly off the slides so attending class is a waste of time. Read the slides to get an idea of what to focus on when reading the book. Try to get another prof. I ended up teaching myself the material.

the course is pretty heavy, but you can study on your own and pass. He says read the text book but it's all on his slides so skip that. the first midterm was so disorganized but i think he learned his lesson because the final was really fair. the lectures ARE boring, and pathology shouldn't be this boring. he can improve his teaching skills a bit.
You must be disciplined and study hard!! The project is very cool actually!  He's very nice and knowledgeable!
SUPER nice guy. Seriously, he is a sweetheart. But I can't lie it was one of the hardest classes Ive taken in my 4 years at Uottawa. You gotta know everything.

He's very passionate about the material thought in class, and knows alot about it! The course topics are super interesting! However, the course load is heavy and lectures can be a bit long, which makes the class annoying. But, ask questions, he always willing to help :), and teacher is pretty good, but the course topic is hard core lol.
All memorization! Most heavy course in university and it's patho, it's not supposed to be like this!! The content chosen is way more heavy loaded than other professors. Very monotone teacher.

TERRIBLE!!! Way too much information to memorize!! Slides are everywhere. No effort to make the class interacting!! Nor tries to help us with the terms, the exam! This is a not a crazy intense class, but with this prof it's literraly a course for scientific expert! Worst prof! Horribly difficult exam!

he has a french accent so it can be difficult understanding him at times. But he's honestly not that bad he really cares about his students and bell curves the quiz, tests and finals scores. Reading the textbook is a waste of time just read the notes underneath the slides and come to class and you'll do fine.

Dr. Leclerc is a nice man, but he probably should be teaching the French stream. He is hard to understand at times.  Midterms & quizzes are difficult & questions are detailed. He's not great at clarifying things and I found the textbook integral to doing well in.  I didn't miss a class but I didn't gain anything by going. I worked hard to do well.
Tough to understand, but a fair guy. Probably should be teaching the french version. An approachable and clearly intelligent prof, just not the best teacher for clarity when explaining material.

Do not take this class with Leclerc. He honestly asks the smallest, most unclear things on his tests and is very hard to listen to and understand in class. He told us what to expect for the midterms/exam and asked us the opposite.

Professor was very boring to listen to and difficult to understand. Read off the slides. Not necessary to go to class. His tests were straight memorization however he asked the smallest and least consequential details. No amount of studying will make you prepared. Without the bell curve I would not have been successful in his class.

Awful professor, however, I learned so much in this class because of the ridiculously heavy course load. If you aspire to be a future health care worker take this class with Leclerc because even though his expectations are impossible you can still get a good grade (average 70%). I learned more in this class than all other HSS courses combined.

I love this class, every part was amazing and I learned a good amount. Took the 3 hour lecture and somehow wasn't bored. Tests are easy, essay is easy if you just put some effort in, and he wil lwork with you. Not a great dude to create dialogue with during class which is the only downside. Take it for sure if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very tough on grade papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Martin was a very fun down to earth professor who focused on getting the class work done as soon as he could while still being funny and having fun. He rarely assigns homework, and only has a midterm and final as his exams. My only complaint is this class was only once a week. I'd take it more if I could!

If I could pick a professor to teach all my CRJ classes, I would pick Prof Martin. Such a funny person and makes class so interesting and fun. I learned so much and enjoyed every minute. Brings in real life situations which is what most CRJ students want, but not all profs do. A really nice person as well and is always willing to help students out

Professor Martin is great. This guy is super cool and has lots of knowledge. The class is based off of 4 things. A midterm test, a small writing assignment, a paper, and a final. His tests are very straightforward and easy. Do good on the paper, that's the only thing he's a tough grader on. A very nice guy ,will work with you.
Has good stories to back up what he teaches and interacts with students a lot. Chill guy.
Beverly Baker is a terrific instructor. She is very knowledgeable and her lectures were very interesting and informative. I highly recommend her!

Incredible! This online English course was one of the most useful courses I've ever taken. Teacher focuses primarily on grammar and punctuation. My writing skills have improved as well. Take her if you want to learn and for an easy grade!
She is a great teacher!!! Really fun and interesting classes!
Awesome teacher! take her! easy to understand and dynamic

If you decide to take this class, DROP IT IF YOU GET THIS PROFESSOR!! She is the hardest evaluator and is never clear with her guidelines. Although she is nice and will help you if you ask, her evaluations are extremely unfair and you will feel intimidated as a student and she will make you feel stupid. This is not a joke.

Overall, this course provided many opportunities to earn marks so it wasn't extremely challenging to get a good mark; however, I found professor Rock's lectures to be a bit hard to follow and confusing at times. The practical sessions were repetitive but I would recommend attending since there are questions about them on the final.
A very inspiring professor with super friendly personality. I enjoyed every single course I have taken with him. Highly recommend for HSS3101 and HSS3110.

I love this prof. Although his lectures seem disorganized, he always takes the extra time to clarify any confusions students have - even if it means repeating himself a few times. He always replies to student's discussion post questions on BS, and overall he's super caring. His class gives you good practice on paper writing +bonus GPA boost!

He's great if you want a GPA boost. The exams and group project are easy and stress-free. However, I didn't really learn much in this class. It was very surface level. It's difficult to focus in class because the lectures are disorganized.

This is probably the best course on research methods. The assignment was a great opportunity to practice the lessons and build confidence in professional report writing. Overall an excellent professor to learn from. He has published a lot of research himself and encourages students with practical examples.

Bishwajit is a really caring and kind professor. He explains everything from a very fundamental level. I will say, this course was kinda repetitive and it is hard to understand what is going on sometimes.
Super caring prof, always responds to emails and takes the time to explain lecture materials outside teaching hours. The lab assignments were easy 20 marks to the final total.

I got very interested in epidemiology after taking this course. Even though it was an online class, he kept the lectures engaging by providing real-life research examples and optional quizzes which helped prepare for the exams. He let students work on individual projects with him to gain first-hand research experience. Highly recommend.

You simply won't learn a thing in this class, genuinely spent the entire semester talking about the same introductory topic. I went into the 3rd year statistics courses feeling extremely unprepared (because I was). Prepare to self study before 3rd year because you'll need it. I've avoided his classes at all costs.

BEST BEST PROF!!!! Highly recommend!!! Labs are super easy, he is so understanding and caring. He makes sure students understand the questions and helps you do well. Exams are fair. No textbook needed. 2 midterms, labs and final. It's a chill class!

Professor Bishwajit is an excellent lecturer, explaining complex topics clearly and keeping us engaged. He goes beyond what's expected to help us succeed, offering personalized support and guidance to ensure every student has the opportunity to excel. His dedication to his students makes him a valuable asset to the University. Highly recommend.
good

It's a 4th year course, so we had two group critical appraisal papers, and one final exam.  Prof Ghose truly one of the best educators I've had the pleasure of learning from during my time at uottawa. His passion for the subject is contagious and caring for students. He always open for discussion, talk about your future plans and current research.

Everyone should take his 4312!!! He teaches students how to critical think and read research papers. We had two major group critical appraisal papers on selected topics from the prof, and one final exam, and easy 20% participation if you don't skip his class. Questions are straightforward and not tricky. One of the best prof at uOttawa health sci.

Prof Ghose's class inspires students to understand the weaknesses and strengths in all types of research papers out on the repositories. His class is not sit there and listen, but students engage the class in active discussions with the prof, so make sure you talk with him :) It's all about critical appraisal.
You can tell Professor Ghose is very passionate not only about what he teaches, but about his students doing well. 100% recommend for HSS 2382.

He made sure that all stress was relieved by all. We were allowed access to all notes during our exams. Labs were an easy 10% and the two group projects were an easy 20% more as long as you did them. There were no calculations, so I would recommend another prof if you prefer that over theory. Such a sweet and caring prof! And the final was online!
Take home exams

Fairly poor lectures but I cannot complain too much given the switch to remote teaching. The real problem was that there was a lot of material on the final that we did not cover, extremely frustrating.

Bo doesn't like teaching and it shows. He is a very smart and I hear he is great as a research advisor. He is like a Lovecraftian god, and is divinely indifferent to your mortal struggles. He is better in office hours, but if you need extra help on the background knowledge of the course he will be dismissive. Likes projects and presentations.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: bonnie is terrible in every sense of the word. the most boring lecturer ever, over complicates things, stumbles her words and confuses people even more, and just over all impossible to keep up with. the content of the class isnt even hard if you understand statistics, she just goes out of her way to make it more difficult and failable.

I enjoyed her lectures, and any grievances for 2321 should be taken up with Terry Klinker, and not her, since he coordinates that particular course. Her teaching style may not be for everyone. Sometimes I felt like lectures were rushed but I learned enough to be successful in the course. She always was happy to help with any questions I had!

Oh man, what words could I use to describe Bonnie Schroeder? Well, besides comically uninteresting, I would describe her as incredibly slow. Grades were supposed to be finalized and in already? Not with Bonnie. No, with Bonnie, its "Your grades will be in Carmen tomorrow!" Well, tomorrow has came, and you can guess what is not in Carmen.

Truly can't say a single good thing about Bonnie. She's insensitive and makes this class incredibly hard for NO reason. The exams truly never reflect what we learned in class or the practice exam whatsoever. Good Luck! Stats 2 is prison…especially with Bonnie.
Hard to say about this course.

Bonnie Schroeder is a special case. I have never met anyone who was as boring or uninspired as her. Lecture is nearly impossible to pay attention to and her lecture videos can only be watched in 2x speed to be tolerable. Some of these were apparently recorded during the great depression and it astounds me how replacement videos were never uploaded.

Really just a doozy. Felt like a prisoner in a gulag entering her lecture. No offense to Bonnie but she is not built for this, I think retirement is the way to go. Not even joking this class is so bad.

Worst professor I've had so far, very boring and monotone. Miserable listening to her talk at 8pm. She's a little over hated, as I haven't had any issues with material and work. 3 group projects throughout the semester, random groups so you better hope for good teammates. Lecture and recitation are mandatory, avoid Bonnie if you can, super boring.
Bonnie sucks. Run far far away to save yourself from this woman. I felt like I am a prisoner being held hostage when listening to her lectures. Save yourself. I repeat save yourself NOW.
This class was unnecessarily hard. The exams did not reflect what you learned. And don't even bother watching Bonnie's lecture videos they are not worth your time you won't learn a thing.

Boring class boring professor boring content. Have insomnia? Stop by her lectures.
Also some girl started sobbing during her exam. Crazy work.
L professor

Unfortunately, my experience with Professor Bonnie Schroeder was less than positive. While she may know the material, her teaching style leaves much to be desired. Her lectures are dry and often hard to follow. It felt like she was simply reading off slides rather than explaining concepts in a way that would help students actually learn. Avoid her!
This class felt so disorganized and was harder than it needed to be. Seeing all the other negative reviews makes me wonder why nothing has changed, like the content isn't even the main problem here.
Bonnie makes y=mx+b confusing
Worst Professor ive ever had in my life, class is extremely difficult

I will be really honest, she isn't even bad, granted statistics is a very difficult class for alot of people, but if you pay attention and do the work, it will pay off. The class work is difficult regardless.

Quite possibly the worst teacher I have ever had, not just in college but going all the way back to my pre-school days.  I would say bad words to describe her but it won't let me.  Don't take her, she is the worst.  She doesn't teach.

I had Bonnie for BUSOBA 2320 and 2321. The BUSOBA department is the absolute worst organized department in Fisher, if not the entire school. I swear Bonnie Schroeder and Terry Klinker saw what Marc Smith was doing, copied it but made everything worse. For the love of all things holy, my final exam building/room was locked and I could not get in.

She teaches everything completely different from the STAT 1430 class and makes everything exceptionally more difficult than it needs to be. I swear she chooses to teach the most difficult ways to reach an answer. I don't understand why she teaches things different from the 1st stat class, makes everything 10x harder to understand.
she makes me want to kms

Gambled away my health for an A. Not worth it. This class is unnecessarily stressful and at the end of the semester I got tinnitus from the stress of this course. Please do extra credit hw and don't believe anyone who says the group cases were easy. They were the bums of their group.

Hearing all the horror stories about this course, I entered with the mindset that time & effort would get me through it smoothly. I was wrong. This was by FAR the hardest & most time-consuming class I have taken in my 3 years at OSU. I cried as I studied for each exam. Bonnie makes everything horrifyingly confusing. Please do the HW extra credit.

this class was a living nightmare. there was about 10% of students who truly knew what they wad doing. whatever u do do not take it by her. She is a terrible teacher. my friends was able to explain the topics better than she ever did. Truly the worst course to take at fisher TRUST ME.  My grade was a b only becasue of the homeoworks
There is a lot of extra credit, and the exams are not as hard as everyone says. However, the lectures are incredibly boring, and one should expect to learn everything on their own.

While her lectures can be hard to pay attention to, the class itself is very well organized, has plenty of opportunities for extra credit, and the exams are extremely fair. She gives plenty of leeway when it comes to earning credit (HWs, extra test questions for bonus, etc.) and gives a few excused absences.

Bonnie's lectures are boring but they are not as bad as people say. If you choose to actively pay attention and try, you will succeed. The content is not difficult; it mimics AP Statistics. Bonnie's teaching is very confusing as she makes the content more complex. There is a ton of extra credit and leeway built into this class.

Quite possibly the worst course I have ever taken at any level of my education. The homework had typos and errors ever week. Bonnie did not submit grades on time and took several days after the hard deadline to post them, JUST TO GET THEM WRONG and email every student that they need an EXTRA WEEK to fix them. We pay 35 thousand a year for this bs?

Ok hear me out. This course is hard. However, Bonnie gives you lot of opportunities to succeed in this class (6% extra credit + curves). If you can build some strong study habits and come to class already having a pretty solid understanding of the material you will do very well. I hated statistics coming into this class, but now I actually like it.
Class kinda annoying basically teach the whole class to yourself. Honestly if you put in the work it's really not that bad.

Worst professor I've had at this school. Was very disinterested and rude during office hours, and she showed little willingness to actually teach students. Exams were challenging, lectures were uninspiring, and the three group projects lacked proper guidance. Tenured, out of touch, and a poor representation of this institution.

Had her for analytics and liked her much better. My TAs were english as a second language which made learning much more difficult. Your group mates are hit or miss on their quality and who grades your project has a big impact on the grade. Schroeder is a nice lady, but boring, just envision your grandma teaching you stats.
Just don't
Bonnie hates her students
Boring lecturer that makes everything much harder than it should be.

Incredibly boring and bad lecturer.The subject matter really shouldn't be that hard, but Schroeder essentially forces you to learn everything on your own as attending lecture was basically useless. I also remember her scolding some people for leaving lecture early even though attending is not required. I don't blame them for leaving early.

Bonnie has an old-school style of teaching that to me was very hard to learn from. You learn more from recitation than any lecture. You are required to watch lecture videos before lecture, then attend lecture where she talks about the same things, and goes on and on and in general, is not nice to students. I would not recommend.
Worst professor at Fisher. Her lectures are all over the place, and I don't think she ever got through all the slides. Exam averages are constantly 70 or below. Needs to retire.
Only take Bonnie if you hate yourself

Bonnie is REALLY BAD at teaching statistics, and I find the group cases to be pretty hurtful overall. I only did well in the class because most of the course content is in AP stats. The class is the poorest put-together I've ever been a part of. Exams start 30 mins after the scheduled exam time. Would not recommend unless you got a 4-5 on ap stats.
I have to say she is the most awful professor I have ever met. She does not explain our confusing group case grade even after class.

By far, one of the most difficult classes I've taken at OSU. Group cases aren't awful, but the exams are tough. Make sure you understand the conceptual aspects opposed to understanding the math (still try to understand the math. The conceptuals take up a large majority of the exam questions.

The worst teacher I've had in my time throughout college. Watching lecture videos and attending in person lectures only confuses you more. She could be teaching simple addition and still confuse her students. Group Projects aren't bad and plenty of points from homework/lecture quizzes. Take another professor if at all possible.
I don't know why Mrs. S has a low rating, she is 10x better than any other professor teaching these courses.
Can hardly understand the way she speaks as she thinks we are still in the 1980s and can't seem to make sense in any of her lecture videos.
Bonnie is the worst professor I've ever had. She expects you to learn very advanced material practically on your own and makes finding support almost impossible

It astonishes me on how you can be a teacher but know so little about actually teaching. The only business she needs to be taking care of is finding another job. Being inside an iron lung is easier than sitting through her class.

Bonnie's lectures can be pretty confusing, but you can get through this class with some effort. The TAs are a big help, and tools like unstuckstudy ai and the textbook make studying easier. Attend class, do the work, and you'll likely get a decent grade.
Just rude!

Extra credit is offered for doing the weekly homework, doing these without statcrunch will help prepare you for exams. I also highly suggest looking over the optional practice (at least the multiple choice portion) to study. Professor Schroeder did a great job and is extremely helpful in office hours and class, you just have to meet her halfway.

Her lectures are the most confusing things in the world, she thinks she is teaching to masters students not people who don't know the content. Worst professor in the entire school and Im not sure how she has a job since everyone hates her.
horrible professor. hasn't used a recently recorded lecture video in ages. bonnie makes everything a lot more confusing

I don't know how Bonnie still has a job after all these bad reviews. She doesn't care about students learning the material at all. If you want any help at all in this class you have to go to the TAs and even then they aren't sure on most stuff. Cstate use to teach this class for credit but Bonnie like always got the university to stop that.

I created an account simply to warn you of the dangers of attending a Bonnie Schroeder lecture.I have PTSD and have awoken several times throughout the middle of the night shaking and crying thinking about monotone,  low energy, empty content lectures.If you have the option to take the class with a non-english speaking professor choose that instead

I don't like to say mean things about professors who seem like nice people, but I have never experienced a worse teaching experience in my entire life. Everything she teaches is made much harder than it should be to understand, while her lecture videos and lectures are both confusing and incredibly monotonous.

Worked really hard in this class to get an A-. Group projects are so hard because nobody understands unless you go to office hours. TAs make this course easier, Bonnie makes it harder. Do your homework, it counts as like 5% extra credit.

Bonnie is a sweet lady, but in my opinion BUSOBA 2320 is a class that she makes quite difficult. She tends to over-explain every topic instead of the baseline knowledge for the exams. Everything you learn in this class tends to relate to real world examples and the 3 group cases you have to do during the course.

Bonnie is not as bad as people put her out to be. She is very knowledgeable about the content, but sometimes I feel like she is too smart to be teaching it at such a basic level. The material is very difficult, but Bonnie does her best to make it clear so that way we can actually learn something. The group cases are a huge hassle though
so hard for no reason

The only reason I have a good grade right now in the class is because of the extra credit you get from homework. Her lectures are soooo long and takes the first half to go over the notes she didnt get to the previous class so it seems like your always playing catchup. The 3 Group projects sucked because no one knew what they were doing.

Bonnie is a kind person, but she is the worst teacher I have ever taken in my life. The lecture videos are the most confusing things ever. Organic Chemistry Tutor and Khan Academy WILL be your best friend. Pray that you have a good TA because Bonnie makes learning this stuff absolutely infuriating. Good luck.

Bonnie was hands down the worst professor I have ever had at Ohio State. Her lecture videos are the most confusing monstrosities to ever exist. Watching them and studying for hours did not help me a single bit as I still struggled. It feels discouraging to ace every class, spend more time in statistics, and are unable to perform well in statistics.

This class took so much time and effort. It is much harder than 1430. If you dont know your terminology (which there is tons of) you will struggle. Its not so much Bonnie being a bad teacher, there is just tons of work not considering you have 4-5 other classes you are taking. Spent 6 hours a week outside of class and still was confused every week.

I spent the whole fall semester of my sophomore year watching her lecture videos. She is not good at teaching the content of the course. The only good thing about this course is that the homework is extra credit. I would never recommend her as a teacher.

I took this class twice, the 1st time i took it was spring of my sophomore year, I was taking a handful of other classes and stopped trying for this class and ended with a D+. The 2nd time I took it was summer going into my senior year, while working a 40+ hr internship I was able to become more committed to the class and ended w/ over a 100%.

F
Bonnie
Schroeder

Worst professor I've ever had and the is the sole reason this course is so hard. Her lectures make no sense and every class is forced to use them. You will have to teach yourself all the concepts yourself. I have no clue how this woman still has a job. Does not give answers in lecture either.

In my opinion, this class was easier than STAT-1430. The majority of this class is hypothesis testing, understanding when to reject and not to reject null hypothesis. So definitely understand hypothesis testing, it will be the case studies and the exams.

VERY generous professor, a ton of easy extra credit opportunities. The best way to ace the exams and case studies is go back and study the homework/quizzes from MyLab. If you do this and write down the equations/concepts on your formula sheet which she allows you to use on your exam, you will at least get a B in this class.

Extreme disconnect between online video lectures, in-person recitation, and the questions presented on the test. Expects you to be able to use statcrunch with minimal explanation and then doesn't allow it on tests. Requires two group projects which are fundamentally incompatible with the way a math class should work.

Overall bad experience.

Professor Schroeder does a fine job at explaining the material. There is mandatory attendance for lectures and recitations, but you are allowed to miss a few. Do the homework for extra credit! As long as you grind out the group projects and study this class is doable! I was able to finish with above a 100, so an A is definitely doable!

Bonnie is a nice person, I read the reviews before I took this course and got Draper for Lec. while having Bonnie for Rec. She's reasonable but I just never spoke during class. Overall, she does need to retire, she literally taught my father back in the early 90's. Aside from this, do good on the group cases, HW, and quizzes as that IS THE CURVE.

Bonnie is actually not that bad. When you talk to her after class, you will know she's actually a really nice person. The concepts are really boring and hard, but there are lots of extra credits opportunities. Be ready to finish the group case ASAP, there will be lots of people during the office hours if you start it late.
Bonnie taught this very easy class really well. She explained all concepts well and gave opportunities for extra credit. Great professor to take for this class.

Bonnie doesn't deserve all the hate she gets as a professor. She knows the material well and does her best to explain it when concepts are difficult. If you approach her after or outside of class, she is very sweet and answers all questions. Her lectures can be dry at times so be careful there.
