Sooo hard to follow what he's saying and he makes everything more difficult than it should be.

he's a really nice guy. very very intelligent and passionate about econ. however, his lectures were quite disorganized and hard to follow and I really wasn't able to learn as much as I wanted. just be prepared to do a lot of reading on your own from the textbook!

He definitely has a great deal of knowledge in economics. He's not great at teaching it though. He just inundates you with information in the lectures, which he seems to think is helpful, but it is more confusing than informative. His class is not hard, it's just annoying because of his lack of organization and clarity.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He really does seem like a nice guy. For real he does. But he's an idiot when it comes to teaching. If you actually want to learn, don't take this man's class. (Even though he's the only 407 professor)

Do not take this class with him. It's pretty clear he has a great understanding of economics, but no understanding of pedagogy whatsoever. Seems like a good person and is passionate about his field, but just simply a horrible teacher at a school where the economics department as a whole is a joke.

good teacher. questions for the midterm and final are taken directly from the prep sheet that he gives ahead of time and from the discussion articles. he also spends alot of time going over those potential exam questions during lecture so if you pay attention the exams will be pretty easy
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to follow, he's not very good at communicating, most of all he makes it more difficult to attach the calculus in an economics class to the principles of economics, so it'll just look like a bunch of random numbers. Worst economics professor so far...

He is a nice guy, but simply can not teach. He stuffers, and can not clearly express what hes trying to say. It makes it very hard to understand what hes trying to explain. He also skips around a lot, so really got focus. Would not recommend
Gives you a great exam prep and a very easy to approach professor. Show up and go to office hours. Will get an A.

If you do your work and study on your own you will do alright. His class was frustrating, unbearable & he is VERY unorganized. Midterm and Final are COPY&PASTE from the review. Takes forever getting just ONE question on a Discussion done. Gave a chance to redo midterm for a small curve but TAKES FOREVER to grade HW's and midterm. Daily attendance.

Well, he's nice and all, but he's not at all good at explaining things. The HW and test questions that he writes are often hard to understand. If you show him that you're trying, you'll get a good enough grade... but you definitely will come out of the class having learned nothing. He may offer extra cred. If you do it you kinda get an A for effort

3 HWs(10%), midterm, final and attendance(5%), discussions/participation (20%). Easy class to pass. Gives you answers to both test weeks before exams. Memorize questions and you'll get at least a B. Go to one discussion and you'll be fine. Not the best teacher but very easy class
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The midterm and final he gave you the questions beforehand and ample opportunities for extra credit. As long as you go to class and engage in discussion you should have no problem getting an A. He sometimes loses focus on the topic at hand. But overall he's a really good guy and willing to help.

The most unclear professor I've ever had when it comes to test questions, never explains any of the questions and expects you to give the exact opinionated answer that's in his head. Takes attendance every day but literally no one in the class ever learned anything from lecture, textbook was useless as well. Learned 100x more in my intro class.

Dr. Bruce is a highly respected professor in the cheme department, seeing as he is the chair. He is kind and lenient. He tries his best to make sure you understand the material, and even though it is a difficult class, he makes it easier to understand. The only reason I did not give 5 stars is he takes FOREVER to grade

Theres a reason Dr. Bruce is the department chair for ChemE. Hes a great guy as well as a great professor. Separations definitely isnt an easy class, but Dr. Bruce does his best to make the material approachable and wants everyone to understand it. Hes willing to work with you whether it be extra help or giving you an extension.

Dr. Bruce is an angel sent from heaven above. He is one of the few professors in the ChE department that is doesn't try to screw you over for his own enjoyment. He explains things well and is very clear as to what you need to know for his exams. As long as you do the homework and ask questions on things you don't understand, you'll be fine.

Dr. Bruce is an absolutely amazing professor. Very helpful during and outside of class and offers good feedback. Very caring and tries to not be too harsh but still wants you to know the material. Only gripe is that he is more elusive than the CIA and FBI are trained to handle. Do not email because you won't reach him.

David is brilliant and knows his subject(s) inside & out. His classes are work-heavy (reading 250+ pages/week) and conference can seem like listening to an essay, but the subject matter is deeply fascinating. He's fantastic in one-on-one conversations and he really cares about his students. His assigned papers were actually fun to write.

David is the most dedicated teacher I've had at Reed. The lengths he'd go to to ensure his students' success are truly humbling. He's also the most well-read professor in the department (other professors have told me this) and has an immense body of knowledge to impart. A wonderful man.

A lot of reading but the reading is actually really interesting from start to finish. Not much work but the work you do asks you to really have a genuine discussion about the class and he gives you a lot of freedom with it. I worked harder and had more fun than I've ever had writing papers for him. Knows his stuff and is a really nice guy.

Brilliant. I have never met someone with the ability to recall such a raw amount of information so easily, and does a great job of contextualizing it. The perk of this is that he is able and willing to discuss absolutely anything relating to the course. You have to initiate conversation, though. He will not think for you, which I thought was good.
david sacks is awesome!  full of funny stories and able to answer any history question.   we read 200 pages a week though so....errrr

I took early modern european humanities with Dave. He is (apparently) extraordinarily well read on his area and a friendly guy outside of class. He has zero idea of how to run a conference or get you to do good work. He is perfect if you have an intense interest in his field and are working one on one.

never had a more mind-numbing class in my life. conference with david sacks is like banging my head against a wall for an hour and twenty minutes. instead of having actual discussions about topics and letting the students guide the class, it's more like 21 Questions with David Sacks--frustrating. brilliant, but borderline incompetent prof.

David generally draws a small serious crowd from what I understand. This is a good thing because "you" get more conference time and the people who are there really want to be there. He will repeat stories, but they're generally funny, but be prepared. Knows the subject matter like the back of his hand.
Amazing prof. The course is about the same difficulty as 2342 but I found it more enjoyable. Highly recommend taking this course as a 3rd year math elective (if not already mandatory).

Diane is one of the best profs I had in university. Very good lectures, she explains everything clearly. Course is well organized with weekly homework to help you keep up. Very nice and friendly towards students. Exams are also very fair and she grades generously. Linear algebra is really important and she made me enjoy it a lot. Would take again.

E 

84

DS EY

A top-notch prof. Her lectures aren't mind-blowing or anything, but all her assessments are very reasonable, and she teaches everything tested. She definitely cared as she even knew most of our names.

Dr. Guignard is easily one of the best professors in the math department at Texas A&M. Tests, homework and quizzes were extremely doable, especially if you go to her office hours for help. If you're able to work out the homework and test reviews by yourself, it should be an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Best prof I've ever had! Dif eq is a tough class, but she taught it in such a way that made it surprisingly easy to understand. She's very organized with her notes on the board and has neat handwriting, which helps a lot. I actually felt like I learned a lot in this class. Go to her office hours! She's super friendly and always willing to help out.

Dr. Guignard is one of the best professors I have ever had. She is very helpful in office hours, and her exams are extremely fair. She actually tests whether or not you know the material, not if you can use critical thinking to solve "special case" problems. She is a diamond in an overall incompetent math department.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Guignard is an awesome teacher, and has extremely reasonable tests. She is one of the most accessible professors I've ever had, and will do anything in order to help you understand more. I will recommend her time and time again.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is pretty reasonable with the assignments. Will let you make up any grades until the end. She will personally help you get better grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teaches to university-level students like one would teach to high school students - and even there, I'm generous! Forming up teams? Finding out a name for that team? Holding up your hand in the air and counting down with your fingers to ask for silence? For Pete's sake, we're adults! And the textbook she used didn't treat us any better.
No Comments

LA ressource si tu as des problèmes en anglais. Elle n'hésite pas à prendre de son temps pour des rencontres privées et elle est a une approche très humaine et empathique. Pour les vrais motivés à apprendre seulement.

People hype his classes up as incredibly hard, but if you pay attention in the lectures and do most of the textbook readings its not that bad. He's a talented lecturer, but you have to be willing to do some thinking. 

The exams are very achievable, and while he doesn't make study guides he makes it clear you just need to know everything discussed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great guy. Office hours are extremely helpful. He helped me learn not only the material (which can be applicable out of class), but also how to go about learning said repertoire/course material (I.e. priorities, what to look for). Readings are long but easy to breeze through with others. Lenient with marking as long as the ideas are presented clear

One of the best, most engaging lecturers currently at the School of Music at UOttawa. His lectures are run like a seminar, so as long as you keep up with the readings and listenings you should be fine. Be sure to participate during class because he places a lot of importance on it. Assignments were fine, but exams are crazy long so study hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Parmer was one of the best academic teachers I've ever had in my ten years of post-secondary education. He made the material absolutely come to life and made it relevant to our lives as performing musicians. He made me work and study super hard compared to other UOttawa courses, but university is supposed to be hard.

Take this class in French and avoid Prof. Parmer at ALL. COSTS. Hardest class I have ever taken and I have a high GPA and this class destroyed it. Unrealistic expectations on exams in terms of quantity and quality of information and does not make expectations clear in terms of what to memorize for exams. Ended up having 27 typed pages for the final

AVOID! AVOID! AVOID! Expectations are unrealistic and never hands out study guidelines! Excessive readings making you read 5-10 pages from the textbook twice a week and making you have a quiz twice a week, one for every reading. The only good thing about him is that he's flexible with hand in dates for project. The absolute worst prof I encountered
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The only somewhat normal thing about this class are the lectures, which aren't bad. Way too much reading and studying requirements before each class (twice a week) for a test you will most likely fail anyway. I don't have much time to practice my instrument, since I have to spend that time memorizing irrelevant "contributors" to Western Music.

Parmer is not only a shocking professor, but a shocking person. His class expectations, as everyone says, are absurd. He believes no one should get A's in university and bombards you with questions that are so obscure you have to dedicate yourself fully to a MANDATORY PROGRAM REQUIREMENT. "The textbook and my lectures cannot be used as resources."
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Parmer is easily one of the worst profs Ive had at U of O, everyone should avoid his class and just enroll in the French History. He is an excellent lecturer but completely throws you off with tests and quizzes. Never takes accountability for low average of class. Also believes no one should get in A+ in uni. Avoid his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While his lectures were engaging and interesting, taking his class was one of the most stressful things Ive ever done. His grading expectations are ridiculous. Im learning French so I wont have to take any more of my required courses with him.

Pros: Great lecturer, makes the content really interesting. Loves opera. Cons: Really tough grader with unreachable expectations. Says no body should be getting A's in University. Be ready to study hard. Do all your readings paying attention to every detail (even pictures). Do your listenings every week. Takes notes in his lectures. Study group.
Unnecessarily difficult Almost my whole class failed a midterm with him. But you will learn with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the best professors I have had. While this class destroyed my GPA, I also learned/retained so much and it reignited my passion for music history. Doing detailed notes of the readings and the listenings/notating the scores by yourself are a must. There is no way you will get a good mark without doing the work. Go to his office hours!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: absolutely brutal final exam.... like actually terrible. I've never cried studying for an exam before but here I am. I did the readings and I'm pretty at risk of failing this class.

Parmer is a great lecturer and his classes are very interesting. However, you need to make sure you do all the readings and study very hard for his exams. He's definitely a tough grader, so be prepared to work harder than your other classes.

I want to cry every time I walk into his classroom. Marks are based heavily on tests. Must do readings every week or you will fail. I don't think he understands the concept that not everybody knows everything about music (like he does) and he assumes you know a lot of pieces off by heart. Not everyone comes from high end music schools.

Tough class but great proff. He communicates the material efficiently and effectively. Study groups are a great tool in his class. Also follow his suggested not taking scheme, the class is geared towards this format. Try re-writing your notes after class. Helps alot in his course.

In all of my many (10+) years of university, I don't think I've ever had a prof with such a bloated ego. His double standards are astonishing: hand in anything late and you instantly fail the class (the only excuse is death), but he arbitrarily cancels classes without warning or explanation. Ego aside, Parmer is reasonably good at teaching.

okay so everyone seems to dread his class. but really, he uses the bellcurve, so  what happens is everyone fails and then is bumped up to a c. this means, if you actually do the work and know how to study, you'll get an A. sure the exam material doesnt always reflect the text or lectures. if you do well on the papers, then you're fine.

Anyone who doesn't like Parmer just wasn't smart enough to realize that he's got a master plan!  If you work hard you'll pass and you'll remember what you learned.  His exams aren't as impossible as people say, just study as hard as you can don't go overboard and be relaxed when you write it.  Ignore his mix and match because they are only worth 10
smartest prof. in the department.  I not only learned and retained course material but also learned great reseach and essay writing skills.  An inspiring man if you don't mind being challenged.
i think the correct word is hypocrite
ummmmmmmmmmmmm talk about a a sentence running allllllll the way to barbados maybe i should type like that it is easier but i would get an F in Parmer's class........

a very bad a good scholar but he is v teach narrow minded teacher doesn't have his own ideas only follow books allows no personal development for the student he is a smart man but he should start thinking independently will make a big deal out of a tiny mistake
Nobody said anything about homework..."Thou dost protest too much"...

Boo-hoo. If you don't like homework, why are you at university? Parmer knows his material very well and is always prepared for student's questions. Class discussion is encouraged, marking is tough but fair, and studying is rewarded. If only the other teachers in Perez had so much academic integrity.
REALITY CHECK: Why?
Best damn prof in the department.
The Professor favors some students rather than the others and he is a hard working man and professor but to much in love with himself I learn more by myself than from him

Learning is alwyas hard work. Parmer likes to think he's hard, he's not. Instead he likes to ask trick questions, anything obscure to make you lose points. That's nasty. Being hard is helping students learn important things, earnestly wanting them to progress, not asking details in a 600 page book.

His class is fun to be in, he goes through the material well and everything, but the real killer is all the extra work that has to be done outside of class time. Also, in the class I was in, our entire mark for the semester was based on two papers and a final, which I thought was unfair.

I really like him, he's a great guy but as a professor, you can never please him. He is very clear as to what you need to do in your exams and such, but the work is overwhelming and you have to keep up in his MANY readings or you will fail. Oh, and he likes to joke about failing- jokes or scare..
Favours students, and ignores others. Marks based on this favouring system. Thinks too much of himself, gets in the way of teaching, otherwise a very smart man.
great prof, fun but hard
hard prob but has good structure and gets things done.  we had some good moments

Professor Tiwari is a very pleasant and kind professor. Although you should not expect university-level mathematics to be a walk in the park, Professor Tiwari offers many resources and opportunities to support you. Assignments were somewhat long; quizzes and evaluations were rather fair. If you are willing to put in the work, you will succeed.

The lectures are a bit hard to follow but recorded and uploaded on Brightspace afterwards so it's not too bad. I found some of her feedback confusing or vague for the essays. The Brightspace is organized by week which is nice to stay up to date on content but if you want to re-read a particular slide deck you have to go back and find it again.
If you follow rubrics to a T you'll still get a bad grade. she knows who you are and only cares about you if you care so show interest and good luck.

Overall she is very nice and willing to help. I personally found the online lectures to be very boring and hard to follow. However she does record them so its nice to look back on. I also found the grading lacked proper feedback and was very vague. The class also had a heady workload relative to my peers who had different professors.

Professor Elena's class is a mixed bag. The lectures can be dry, but she provides clear guidelines and is happy to clarify concepts. Using unstuckstudy alongside the free textbook helped me stay on top of the workload.
Her online lectures are boring and tedious and her brightspace is poorly organized. On the other hand the class itself is easy to get a good grade in.

Elena is a very nice professor. She has a passion for her subject that makes learning much more enjoyable. She posts weekly briefings that detail the learning plan, so students can be prepared. There are 2 textbooks, but they are not mandatory (I didn't get them and did fine). Additionally, she is available for questions outside of class.

I don't understand all the hate, she's actually a lovely professor! Her course material is very straightforward which I really appreciate, and none of her assignments are "tricky", just simple and useful. She even provides us with templates and rubrics for everything, so we know EXACTLY what to do and how.

She's such a G. I took her during the summer and you can tell she loves English and teaching. Everything was fairly straight forward. I considered her an easy marker because the things I wrote were not my best work but she always gave me 80% or more and her feedback was good. If you go to class she literally gives you everything you need to succeed

She's not an amazing professor, but she's not as bad as everyone says. Yes, it is true you will have a lot of things to read, her lectures are dry, and her expectations are very high. However, getting an A or at least a B+ in her class is not difficult. Will I take her class again? No, but I do recommend her if you don't have any other options.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly, she really does care about her students but you have to show interest in her class. Do so by emailing her your questions and requesting Zoom meetings. I do not think she is a tough grader but start your formal report early since it does take a bit of time.

She might be caring and kind during the lectures, however do not let it fool you into believing that she'll be generous with the grades. She is extremely tough at grading and she finds it hard to stick to the rubric designed to grade the assignments. I would say try and avoid her if you can.

Her skill builders were awful, her teaching awful, the way she graded and couldn't open PDFs like a regular being and not gas light me for submitting a warped document, awful. She told me I was going to fail and drop out, after this I was certain I was getting an A+, fast forward, after a lot of sucking up I got away, but don't get stuck. BE WARNED
She's a really nice person and very passionate about what she does which makes the class more engaging, but the workload is a lot compared to other classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She's not as bad as everyone says but she's not perfect either. In class she's a really nice and caring lady and explains the topics well, and everything is posted on brightspace so no issues there. However, she's a very tough grader. But I'm not sure if it was her or the TA's marking the assignments... Last thing, by email she is quite cold...

Terrible Teacher. she just doesn`t care about the students at all. She will give you assignments and any questions you have, she will tell you to look at the slides she posted. Literraly unaproachable by email, she will tell you to bring your questions to class, but when you do, she wount bother answering any of them.

Would not recommend taking her classes. Consists of 5 group projects which you only receive your group the day it is due. Discussions on assignments and how to do them the day they are due as well. So many useless novels and short stories to read that have no significance to assignments. Tough marker and doesn't follow the rubric she gives you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Please try to avoid her, otherwise you would regret it. Next year, you will take the communication skills course which your professor will only teach you about 5 hours in total due to he believes that you have already learned all the knowledge in this course. Actually, you did not because what she taught you is not what she marks your work.

there were 3 assignments. I started them all the day they were due. Put in 5-8 hours of work for each. The TAs are kinda useless, they just read off of slides but they also do the dgd work for you which is nice. I didnt really listen to the lectures at all just took notes once a blue moon.
Very easy professor gives clear marking schemes and assists at any time. Take her class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Ilina prepares you for every assignment she gives. Every week you get an assignment that you do in class together, and they're only marked on participation. As long as you show up to class, it's an easy 100 on each of those assignments. The midterm was easy, and as long as you put in the work for the assignments they are also easy.

This prof was extremely unprofessional throughout the entire semester. She would constantly remind everyone in class about the rubric for assignments, then would not use them to grade. She was extremely rude when you asked for additional help by email. Add on fact that she is extremely boring while teaching, and you will hate this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She's very unapproachable and an extremely tough grader. The lectures are useless and when youd ask her a question she would tell u to check the slides and thats it.

She's a very harsh person in her emails, the lecture slides are not helpful, and the lecture itself is so boring but the attendance is 10% so you have to be there, there's always a lot of reading to do. A VERY THOUGH GRADER, avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She was very aggressive in her verbal approch to students and very unapproachable Prof. Very harsh and not empathetic for grades and assignments. Once faced with an altercation unfairly grades her students as if it is a punishment. Very unresponsive with emails. Would never have the professor again, terrible experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very good teacher. She makes the lectures and DGDs very fun. She is definitely a harder marker for the DGDs than the TAs though.

A LOT of readings to do before every class. Calls you out. She doesn't make assignments clear, then gives a bad grade for not doing what is expected. Lectures are extremely dry and unorganized. Attendance is 10% of your grade. Avoid if possible!!

Her lectures are so boring and you cannot hear her if you don't sit in the front. My TA is a terrible teacher and cannot explain much. Lectures are useless and we go over extremely basic concepts such as a resume or a formal letter. Learned this stuff in grade 8. Avoid this prof
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She gives a lot of extra help and out of class help, but she is so unbelivably confusing. I find all her lectures hard to follow and when she explains concepts to me I'm left with more questions than when I started. She also has arbitrary grammar tests that don't seem to reflect report writing skill at all. She is a very tough grader.
I sent her emails but she did not answer any of them. She is stright and hard to get along with. I am pretty sure that I will not take this course again.

elena cares about her students and if you're in her dgd group, you'll see that she's a funny and cute lady. launchpad was really annoying though - no other class had to do that + all the assignments. she is a tough grader and very specific even tho the assignments are easy. go to her office hours for tips. u rlly gotta put in effort!!

She is a great professor, very caring like a strict mom, and posts the notes online so the information is accessible. The course is not too hard, only the launchpad assignments are hard. However, DGDs are mandatory so always arrive five minutes earlier.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: She is really an amazing prof. Everything is clear and the grading is not that tough.

She is very confusing to understand when it comes to her assignments. If you go to her office hours and ask questions about your assignment, she will sit down and tell you how to perfect it. But when you fix everything up, she will still give you a 60 on an assignment. She doesn't care about her students and very tough with marks. Avoid her.
Marvellous Prof, although her launchpad assignments are hard.
She is a great professor because she understands students and is willing to help. However, her LaunchPad Grammar tests are really hard but other assignments are easy. Be ready to work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best teacher for the technical report writing class! She treats you like an employee, with everything building towards your final report. You're taught how to make employment documents and then various types of report that all support the final. Very useful for any engineering student!

As stated by others she marks pretty hard. I think its just because she has her own set of expectations for university students. Very caring a compassionate prof, super nice person. Easy to level with. Lectures were honestly not engaging to be honest, they're a little too slow paced. Assignments are definitely doable from content on her website.

For most assignment the guidelines are very clearly provided. Sample papers, scaffolds are given for most pieces Eg. sample memos, scaffolds for research proposals etc. In fact, you can skip lectures and do assignment solely based on the provided scaffolds and materials and by reading guidelines. Teaching assistants provide good feedback.

She's a tough grader. I do hope that the works are graded fair and square but unfortunately not. She gives very vague feedback and she doesn't explain the grades given. When she makes a mistake, she doesn't apologize. I appreciated her time given during the office hour several times, but she decided to give me attitudes instead.

The prof is super nice and caring. If you have a problem for submitting by a due date, go in advance and she will be super compassionate and give you the best solution. Even though she knows a student has great potential, she marks tough no matter what. Also, she is super funny! She gives great feedback, but her expectations are tricky sometimes.

Professor Ilina will give you very specific instructions on how to do an assignment, and then proceed to grade you based on a completely different set of imaginary standards. She stresses the importance of checking your work for typos, and yet her slides and emails are riddled with errors. Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: We didn't have any exams- just 4 assignments and some weekly online quizzes. Really easy assignments, I don't think I did any of them before the night before they were due. Knows that making science and engineering kids care about grammar and writing technicalities isn't easy, but still makes it seem slightly less boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Elena's lectures covered very useful concepts, and I do feel I am a stronger writer after having taken her course. However, she can be a very frustrating professor to have at times. She gives out far more assignments and quizzes than any other prof teaching the same course. Take her class if you want to learn, avoid her if you want an A+.
Really tough grader, if you have the chance , do not have her as the prof

Don't go to class. Its never been more pointless. She just talks and talks about the assignments but I usually just asked my TA about those. The material she teaches in class is so pointless and its all for the grammar tests that you do in the DGD. Overall, extremely nice professor but extremely boring.

Professor Ilina makes you work for the mark.  However she is very accessible in her office hours and gives very good feedback on where to improve.  Overall if you put in the work and get her feedback on assignments you can get a fairly good mark.  I was never great in english but still managed to get good grades with Ilina's help.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Great prof, definitely recommend her for ENG1131! Really nice lady and explains everything really well. Her assignments and grammar quizzes are not hard and you can easily get a good mark if you follow the concepts learned in class. Discussion groups are mandatory, I was in her group and she gave really good feedback on all the assignments.

Elena's a very thorough lecturer but the course is relatively easy (lots of basic grammar) so it's hard to make it interesting. She does a good job though. Very caring, will answer any and all questions you have. Don't be late to class (if you go).

She's not a bad prof, but she's not a good prof either. I literally went to two lectures the whole semester because she posts everything on Blackboard. Her explanations for certain concepts are long and most of them are common sense. The DGDs are mandatory; this is where the actual learning happens and quizzes are given.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you have a chance to have her as a teacher, do so. The workload is surprisingly light, as she gives no final exam. She only grades the papers you hand in. The textbook helps a lot while writing the papers, so I suggest you buy it. DGD's are mandatory, although it is not necessary to go to the lectures. She posts everything on blackboard.

Professor Ilina herself is not a bad prof, but she can be a little condescending. I find the actual content of the class to be a bit of a joke. You can easily do all the papers without going to the lectures at all. She posts everything on Blackboard too, which is nice.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: She doesn't know very much about what she's talking about, very rude to most students in class, pointlessly talks about stuff everyone should know wasting class time, try and switch out if you can. Probably one of the worst English profs out there. She seems like a nice enough person overall but very bad at teaching.

She is a very good prof. She took the time to make it clear what we had to do only projects and made herself available to help students on a one on one level. She also played music for us in the mornings before lectures. Just make sure you do the assignments the way she asks and the course should go well. Also there is alot of group work in the DGD
Really tough grader. If you cross her, consider yourself done; she grades those whom she likes more lenient than others.
She's a real gem but her classes aren't really geared to preparing you for an assignment. She will show you some examples but you'll never has access to them.

She's a nice prof, but she makes you work for the marks. As long as you put in all the effort required, you should come out with a decent grade. Slacking off and procrastination will leave you with a D at best. She treates you like you're in elementary school: takes attendence, no phones, no earphones. She's a kind prof who cares about her students
SHE IS THE BEST
JUST AMAZING
She is a nice person and always helped me when I asked, if you aren't illiterate than you can get an easy B+ AT LEAST.

Elena Ilina is a good professor who unfortunately has to teach a class that no one wants to take. For my program this course is mandatory, but very useful later on.  This course prepares engineering students for the types of documents that we will be encountering in the work force.  Elena is very clear on what she wants from you each assignment.
She's a nice person. If she is a high school teacher, I would give her a A+. She treated us like children. Pls give us higher mark to let us study other subjects.

I'm not sure why Elena gets so much hate from some people on here. She taught the course clearly and tried to make it interesting along the way. If you don't like the lectures because of the content, then don't go to them. I attended very few and still received an B+ in the course. There's free participation marks at the DGD's... just go to those.

Elena is eager to help students during lectures, discussion groups and her office hours! The grading criteria for assignments is clear, and in-class quizzes are easy and open-book. The lectures are rather long and boring, but Elena does try her best to make them less dry. The assignments are also relevant to engineering careers, which is great!

Great prof but a hard prof. With the content of this course you really can't expect to be on the edge of your seat the entire class but Elena tried. Most of the negative reviews here are from the people who won't last in engineering anyway so if you're a good student and can pay attention take Elena's class and get Gemma as a TA!

English on its own is a very boring subject. Prof Elena tried so hard to make it fun. She played music at the beginning of class to keep people awake but no one ever danced. Honestly , I feel like there's nothing she can really do. I mean it's English. Plus, she's really approachable and always willing to help.
Lays out a simple step by step process to complete assignments
bad

Good prof for sure.. She's not perfect but she definitely tries her BEST. She doesn't give up free marks why some people are mad at her, but she helps you get the knowledge you need to get a good grade.

Fair Professor, easy course. Zero creativity required. If you follow the appropriate conventions , you will excel in this course. Also Gemma is the best TA ever.   Elena gives you all the tools you need to succeed but you still need to put in the effort, obviously. She is very helpful if you put in the time and effort. Dry lectures, however.

The course itself is not that interesting but the assignments were quite relevant to the engineering profession. Elena was  clear on what technical aspects she expected on the assignments and didn't care about the actual content. To do well in the course just take the assignments and homework seriously and put in the time. If you do its an easy A.

Professor Ilina is always there if you need her. All you need to do to not get a bad mark is to go to her office hours and talk to her, she will explain 1 on 1. Great sense of humor, and her tests are open book, which are an easy A if your IQ is higher than 10. Do NOT RECOMMEND taking this class to those who are NOT in engineering though!
I am done with English now so I am happy but I did not enjoy the class.

Elena Ilina is the worst professor I have ever had. This review comes after she emailed her entire Fall 2015 class claiming she was "deeply wounded" by her reviews on this website. These "negative" reviews are accurate reviews. Very disappointed in Elena's professional conduct. I would advise that any student taking ENG1112 stay away from her class
Please switch your prof right now, please.

She is very thorough with her lectures. Although some of the slides are summaries of the textbook, she adds a lot of her own insight, which helped a lot! Her assignment sheets are a little vague sometimes, but a quick email helps clear things up! Grammar tests are open book, and some are feebies if you attend the DGD that day! Love her humour!

Elena did a great job conveying all the material in the one class we had a week- which happened to be Monday morning at 8:30. Elena provided great feedback on my papers and was always available to help! She made the expectations clear on the reports and they were very reasonable!

Prof. Ilina was was clear, concise, and very fair with her marking scheme. The quizzes and assignments, although elementary in nature, were useful in solidifying a concrete foundation for English writing in a technical environment.
Wouldn't recommend this prof for this course.

She's an OK professor. My largest qualm with her was that she did not use the board enough. To me, a good professor is seen by the examples they do at the board, not in their powerpoints.  On the upside, her criteria are clear. In addition, if you go see her with a draft of your assignment, then she'll give you some good tips on how to improve it.

Elena is always there if you need help. Struggling on an assignment? Do not be scared to email her for some help. If you show you are interested and want to learn then you will do just fine. Do your homework before tests and you will do well!
The most practical immediately applicable class I have taken so far.  Isn't the most interesting material but has clear grading criteria and I had a good TA.  Put in the time will get an A. (rhyme)

By far my favourite class I took last semester. The writing skills learned and the types of documents in relation to this course will prepare you for many different professions.  I found Dr. Ilina very clear on what was expected for each assignment. She also gave many opportunities for participation marks. Over all great professor and great course!

Good class- Elina is hilarious and very helpful. Answers questions well in lectures and works one on one with students to help them get a better grade. Really good class for science/ engineer students. In my opinion, Elina was great. She made 8:30 lectures on La Friday morning not only bearable , but interesting and fun as well. Highly recommend

Lectures are useless (unless you wanna know about pronouns). assignments have nothing to do with what we "learn" in class. Really hard marker and no matter how much effort you put in the assignments she will give you max 80% on it. Hate English class. TAKES ATTENDANCE.

Entertaining lectures, mostly participation marks (for grammar "tests"), put some work into the class and you'll do well. TA was helpful.  On another note, got an A+, attended all the lectures, aced the actual grammar tests, and got casually accused by her (not the TA) of plagiarism on the final paper. So yeah, that was interesting.

Rude and annoying. Class is interesting and useful for the sciences / engineering. However, don't pick that prof. She's useless, unclear and her classes are sooo boring. Her assignments are so vague and you don't even know what to write or what she's looking for. She takes attendance every class to make sure that people don't skip (or no one comes)
Lectures are long and boring but Elena is hilarious... And everything is posted on blackboard. Generally easy course.
Lamo shes a delight
Awful professor. Very rude to students, not clear at all and just unpleasant to be around. Avoid at ALL costs. Honestly a shame she is employed by the university.

Terrible teacher, can't explain anything you ask. Completely useless to approach in her office hours because she can't explain herself correctly and just refers you to the text book. DO NOT CHOOSE THIS PROF! Super boring lectures too.
The worst prof I've ever seen. She is really rude to her student. Try to avoid her.
Overall a good class. Prof Ilina explained necessary concepts well, but still found there were some tough markers.

Elena is an "old school" professor who rightly doesn't tolerate disrespect. Many complain about the mandatory workshops but honestly, if you just read the chapter before, you'll do well. Participation is very important and even if you answer incorrectly, she'll point you in the right direction and push you until you get it right.

She has very strict rules (ex. cannot be late for workshops) and is very old-school in that matter. However, she provides all the help you need to get an A in the course. Follow the instructions and go see her during her office hours. She basically guides you to what she wants, so how can you go wrong?
She makes a very boring class less boring.

Elena is a great professor! She is very clear in her grading criteria and makes herself available outside of class to look over assignments and give you feedback. You don't need to go to lectures because she puts everything on Blackboard; however, attendance to DGDs are mandatory.  The final exam is take-home!

This is by far the most boring class I've taken so far. Honestly, don't bother going to class because it's not worth it; however, make sure to go to every DGD and hand assignments in or you won't pass. Follow the samples online, don't bother buying the textbooks and act like you're paying attention in the DGD and you'll get a good grade.

Get into a DGD that she doesn't teach if you can. Look at the examples posted online and follow their structure for assignments. Don't bother attending lectures until the last couple weeks when the Final Report is being discussed. Skip the Beer textbook. The Diana Hacker textbook is helpful for in class quizzes and APA citation.

Elena Ilina was not the greatest prof ever. She has the pleasure of teaching one of the dullest classes that one can take. Also, her slides can contradict what is labeled as "correct" in the text book. This gave a great feeling of confusion when working on assignments. DGD's were good and it was an easy class. I'm glad that this class is done!

When I read the negative comments about her, I was terrified to be in this class. Let me just say, this turned out to be one of my favourite classes! She's quite friendly if you treat her with respect (as you should for any professor) and she wants her students to do well. Loved the Discussion Groups and the T.A was super nice! Would take again.

AMAZING TEACHER. Class was from 7 to 10pm on Mondays and she managed to make the class interesting. Loads of information but she makes everything very clear and her explanations are filled with examples. Very caring. Would defenitely take again.

Professor Sylvia is a very understanding and intelligent prof! She was easily accessible outside of class and provides great feedback. The structure of the course is well thought out and every assignment leads to the final project. She also offers a bonus percentage for completing the syllabus quiz for easy marks!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed having Eliza as my comms prof and would reccommend to other students.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Sylvia is incredibly kind and knowledgeable. She cares a lot about her students and her class was always the highlight of my week. Her class format was unique, having us work in class and watch lectures online. Her class is easy because she is good at teaching & encouraging students to put in the effort, she prepares us well to succeed.

She is fantastic. Very approachable and funny. The majority of the grades are assignments that go toward your final paper. She is an easy grader up until the final assignment. There are weekly quizzes based on the readings, but you have unlimited time and two tries. She is amazing and I have learned so much from her!!!!

She was very understanding of my academic accommodations, which is rare for professors. She went above and beyond to make her students feel heard and ensure they are staying engaged in lectures. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Nice professor, free Tims were available during the last lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Sylvia is kind and cares about her students and work. She is dedicated to providing students with great feedback as well as providing them with appropriate knowledge and feedback. Very accommodating and respectful.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great teacher tbh, always willing to help you. Class is not hard at all if you put in a little bit of effort. Fun to talk to and quite the looker!

Loved her so much that I made sure to get her again the next semester. We are not just numbers to her and she really makes sure that everyone understand and participate. She can be a little desorganised from time to time but thats it.

Very friendly and engaging professor who enjoys the material she teaches. Gives students many opportunities to do well. May be a little flustered at times but doesn't detract from the learning. Tests are fair. There's a moderate amount of homework but that can be expected with any language course.
She really enjoys and takes pride in her work making her one of the best  professors around. Strongly recommend.
She has a great interest in the success of her students! Very helpful, friendly, and approachable. Awesome teacher.
Professor Quinn asks a lot of her students but also provides enough support that academia feels accessible and open to everyone who tries hard. Hard but good class.

While there was a lot of reading to do for this class, the small number of assignments made the course relatively light. Quinn gives plenty of creative liberties to students for essays, however her grading is hard; you won't get an A+ unless your work is 'good enough to be published in a journal'. All books are expected to be purchased by students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very boring & useless lectures; you don't need to attend. No feedback given (which is required considering her harsh grading)

Tough grader. 
She makes her points very clear in her lectures, but the big essays are a little daunting to do.. attending class does not lead to good grades. A lot of self teaching to do and you have to really put it a lot of effort to get good grades.
However, the grammar quizzes were very very easy. skip the grammar part of her class

- Examples in slides did not add up to the difficulty of the questions being asked on later quizzes
- She didn't provide great feedback in personal zoom meeting. Was a lot of self teaching.
- Dense slides made it harder to study.
- Fair grader but she was hypocritical to some of her guidance I received in a zoom meeting.
- Would not recommend.
Boring lectures, skip them. Grammar quizzes every week that are easy. Lots of little assignments, couple big essays. Easy marker.

Dr. Petrova is a tough grader- but she is accessible if you make the effort, super personable, and happy to offer extra help. I do think she has high expectations compared to other profs for first-year, not necessarily an easy course... if your goal is anything above a B, I recommend office hours! Seeking extra feedback made a big difference

the class overall isn't terrible ig, like if you passed high school English you should be good. dr petrova is pretty mundane and topics are fairly boring. there are weekly quizzes, a few minor assignments, 1 midterm and 2 essays. the biggest issue was hard marking and unclear feedback. not very helpful and guidelines are VERY unclear.

IMO Dr. Petrova is a pretty good prof. The lectures were pretty boring and I was tuned out for most of them but if you read the slideshows and know how to write an essay in coherent English you should be fine. The grammar quizzes weren't difficult and she is also very available outside of class to answer questions and give essay feedback.
I enjoyed class with Dr.Petrova. She makes the content easy to follow and as long as you interact in the meeting when she asks questions you should be good for the weekly grammar quizzes.

Not sure why her reviews are negative, she is a really sweet prof that wants you to succeed. She did only read off the slides, but she posts them so no need to go to class since attendance isn't taken. Easy weekly grammar quizzes (takes 30 mins max), 2 essays, and no exam. No need to buy the textbook IMO, easy A if you are literate.
The class does get boring at times but pretty easy to follow. There are grammar quizzes each week. But yeah the class being online and late at night did not help
Most boring professor I've ever had, avoid taking her. Easy class but the most boring professor, she simply reads of the slides and yet the lectures and mandatory.

She told us our textbook would be used every class, I paid way to much for a book I Never even touched, Id email her about a problem and get a flat response or she would "answer" my question by replying with another question. The lectures are just her reading slides. Her Grammar quizzes were awful, she made no sense half the time... do not take it!

Was not an easy class for me. I did not learn anything from this class. She didn't give proper feedback a lot of the time. Everything was so ambiguous, especially the essay structure. The lectures are just her reading the slides. We did nothing with the textbook. There were two essays and we had weekly grammar quizzes and assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: This prof is painfully boring and the lectures were the worst part about my week becuase of how boring they were. Also my TA was impossible to get office hours with as she did not even like in ottawa (also she was lowkey kinda rude). Do not take classes by this prof unless you want to hate everything about your life
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy class, generally had one grammar quiz and one short assignment per week. Classes were a bit boring as she was just reading off slides but she always made sure to answer people's questions. Quizzes were very easy to do if you actually take the time to read the slides she uses for the dgd. Only downside was class time (early morning).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: save yourself from this professor and DONT take this course with her.

Don't be misled by the negative reviews. The class is easy, but there's there's slightly more homework than you would expect. Some of the quizzes are more difficult than the teaching material lets on. She takes the time to answer questions and make sure people really understand the material in her lectures. Kind lady with a clear love of writing.

This is my first class with this prof and most definitely my last. The grammar quizzes are so hard along with the weekly assignments due. I'll be lucky if I get over a 50 in this class. Save yourself the tears and don't take this prof.

The weekly class meeting is nominally answering questions, but actually chatting with students. She responds to emails quickly but never directly helping students solve problems. The assignments are graded extremely harshly, and I would guess that only students with Shakespeare's writing skill level would get an A+.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Booooooooring. Just so so so SO boring. However, it is a very easy class where you do the work and pass for sure even with a pretty good mark.

Tough grader! Corrections are very generic and advice consists of questions. Avoid! Gives weekly assignments due every Mondays yet class and the day she talks about the material with the class (synchronously) is on Thursday.

Petrova is a horrid professor for ENG1100. Firstly, this class being online probably had something to do with how bad it has been, but the unclear grading, ridiculous grammar quizzes/powerpoints and assignment expectations have ruined this class. At least she's nice.
She did not provide support to the student that needed help with grammar. Her ta is tough and gives 40 and 60 to people that do the work.
She's a very boring and monotone lecturer

This is one of those silly required classes the school makes you take. Not interesting at all, but I suppose that isn't entirely her fault. She is friendly, but will take points off on papers for things most profs wouldn't (eg small gramamtical mistakes). I'd avoid this class unless you really want help with basic aspects of essay-writing.
Boring, dull, uninteresting. Easy A, but my friends got pretty low marks from her for unknown reasons.
A nice professor but VERY boring. The DGDs are a lot more interesting to go to, and I'm not kidding when I say the lectures are EXTREMELY boring.
boring english class, but the prof was very nice! she encourged people to participate and she lectured well..marked easy
Great prof!! Very helpfull and if you came to class, did the readings and participated, you would do well.
very boring classes...but she was nice and tried to get people to participate

It was an ok class. With the essays I hated them because she never seemed please. Her class though is really involved, but you never really feel like you got the answer right. Over all easy mid-terms and exams if you read the texts and show up to class.
The class itself was boring, but this Prof had a lot of interesting info to share with the class.

She brings quite a bit of philosophy to class, which is fun, and her teaching style is good.  A little bit too lecture-y for my tastes (I prefer more discussion, instead of "anyone remember this?  Yes?  Good--here's what it means"), but still quite good.

Only a 40% midterm and 60% final which was very stressful. The midterm (memorization) was harder than the final (critical thinking). He records lectures but doesn't allow laptops to take notes. Prof is very passionate about his work and he was able to change my world view throughout the course. I recommend him just so you can listen to him speak.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Was a great teacher, good at lecturing. Content heavy. Exams are closed book in person, if you study you will pass. Do need to do the readings from the course manual. He does not allow technology in class, but does record the classes.

I believe Professor Oscapella is a good professor. Exams are doable, attendance is required to do well on the exams, and the class is entertaining. 

Two drawbacks. a) the professor pushes his own material, which is quite expensive for what itis, and b) the professor is openly pushing a lib political agenda and expects students to regurgitate it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Super happy to see that he might still be teaching this course at uOttawa. I took this class around 5 years ago and he was a fantastic, passionate, and well-informed professor. His exam was no walk in the park, but if you know the material through and through it will be fair to get that A+.

one of my favourite profs. i have learned so much from him; the course is worth taking! Lectures are long, but honestly, if you just sit, do your readings, and pay attention (i rarely took notes), u will do well! i wish he taught more courses... he is really caring and although the exams r heavy, it's not hard to retain information. luv u oscapella

There was only a midterm and final exam and the grading was extremely tough. However, when he lectures you can see how much he cares about the topic and he is very knowledgeable. Made a 7-10 class very tolerable. Would definitely take him again.

He's a wonderful prof that genuinely cares about the subject and tries his best to get the main messages through. Midterm was 40% and final was 60% so there's not much to spread your grades out with, which is only reason why I wouldn't take again. His ppts include mostly examples, I suggest getting the course reader if you want the main ideas.

The material is not as interesting as it seems, Prof Oscapella is very knowledgeable, but his lectures are not very organized and seem only like a collection of anecdotes related to the topic. It's extremely difficult to take organized notes The midterm is tough, but if you study well and do your lectures you should get an ok grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, he knows what he is talking about but really expects highly from students on the midterm and final. the course is so lecture heavy, with so many slides in his lectures, you don't really receive an exam review, the course is graded on two exams in the course,  take this course at your own risk, your GPA will drop for sure!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Best prof at uottawa. He genuinely cares about his students and is passionate about what he teaches in his lectures

Amazing dude, really interesting material but really heavy lectures. Guy knows what he's doing though cause I still went to every single class. Grading criteria are pretty strict but I don't hold that against him cuz he knows his stuff and he's passionate about what he teaches to the point where it is contagious.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes a nice guy but his lectures are so long. Bit of an overwhelming course in terms of readings (almost 100 pages a week) but he knows what hes talking about. Class is only graded by a 40% midterm and 60% final which is stressful

eugene is a complete G. my mental health was at its lowest last semester and i couldnt even bring myself to write the final paper (was supposed to be about 10-12 pages), and so i sent him an email apologizing for handing in barely anything for the final and he still passed me with a D, when i was prob at a 30 in that class. really cares!

Hands down one of my all time favourite professors and class I've ever taken. Lecture heavy but the content and the way he gives the lectures made it interesting I actually enjoyed going to his classes. If you have a general understanding of the concepts and can make links between them you'll get a good mark, he's very clear with what is important

He is such a sweetheart. So kind and caring, and extremely knowledgeable on the topic of drug policy. He really makes it interesting by drawing on current events. I would 100% recommend taking this class!

Prof. Oscapella is the best professor I've had at UOttawa. Hands. Down. He is so passionate and knowledgeable about drug reform that it's motivated me to go into drug policy. Definitely need to go to class as attendance is 10% but I actually looked forward to going to class every week!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lots of reading, lots to study, all worth it

One of the best professors at the university!  His lectures are amazing and very engaging. Out of all the classes i've taken so far I have learned the most in this class. His exams are a little tough but as long as you do all the readings and show up to class you will get a fair mark. I highly recommend to take a course with him.
Awesome prof! I highly recommend you take his course - he is SO smart and presents really interesting stuff.
Amazing lecture, must do!

This was by far the best class I took at UofO! Should be mandatory.. Oscapella is so passionate about what he does & it shows! Midterm was pretty hard, but if you do the readings & attend class you will do great! The course itself is super interesting & he is so knowledgable. Overall an amazing class!

BEST TEACHER I'VE ENCOUNTERED AT U OF O HE'S DEEPLY PASSIONATE IS WHAT HE DOES. HIS MIDTERM IS LITTLE HARD AND READINGS ARE A LITTLE LONG,HOWEVER THE FINAL MAKES UP FOR IT. HE'S FUNNY, MEDIA PRESENTATION ARE INTERESTING AND AN OVERALL NICE TEACHER. BEST CLASS I'VE TAKEN SO FAR AT U OF O
This professor is excellent! In my university career, I learned the most from this class. Work hard, and get a good fair grade at the end.

Absolutely amazing professor. Attendance is mandatory - there is a sign in sheet for most classes. His midterm is tough, but if you make notes from the readings, and dig through the important parts in his lectures, you'll end up doing okay in the end. The final exam will salvage your mark.

I LOVED this class. I recommend this class to everyone! Oscapella is exceptionally knowledgeable, and clearly very passionate about criminal justice and drugs. He is extremely helpful, and very willing to answer any questions. And unlike other prof's, he is willing to hear opinions contrary to his own. This was definitely my favourite class at uO!

One of the most dedicated profs I have ever experienced. He is so passionate about educating society on drug policy, and it had really opened my eyes on laws. I highly recommend this class, though you will not receive a good mark.. He is very specific on answers, if you miss class you are screwed. A lot of information to take in and remember!

Amazzzzzing man and professor. The degree of work he has put into the field of irrational drug policy is unbelievable. Just listening to him speak is enjoyable. Best class at the University of Ottawa.

Everything everyone is saying is true! Great prof teaching a phenomenal class... Midterm is tough but don't get discouraged, exam is marked a lot easier to make up for lost marks. You'd be crazy not to take this class! By far the most interesting class at the U of O!

VERY VERY VERY INSPIRING. Watch out the mid-term exam is tough... be very straightforward with your answers and do not leave anything beyond and you should be okay. The class is interesting however repetitive but if you actually put effort into the class youll get an A.

Loved this professor and loved this class! He turned me into quite the drug policy debater with my friends. An expert on the topic and very clear in his lecture. Midterm is difficult as he wants specific answers but the course is still definately work taking just for an eye-opening experience. He's cute for an old guy too :P

Best professor at U of O teaching the best class at U of O. It should be mandatory for every student on campus to take Crime and Drugs. He has made me want to base my career around this topic. Very inspiring, excellent lecturer.
you need to be very specific when answering questions on his mid-terms. if you dont give him the answer he wants you don't get any points at all.

Very good prof. His passion for his work and his extensive knowledge about his field offer great insight into the failure of the drug war. The midterm (marked by TAs) was rough, but he offers a fair chance to improve your mark on the final. Great Prof! Take this class!

Epic class. Have made use of his course pack for 4 papers in different courses. Is even willing to give you additional information if you're writing on the subject. Midterm is a bit of a surprise so make sure you study specifics but final is essay format-very fair. So passionate about the material and so anti-Harper you can't help but love him.

Phenomenal. Graduated in 2005, but use his lecture material all the time to shut people up re: the war on drugs and how it should be fought. Make sure you are THOROUGH when you study for the midterm and final!
Best crim prof at U of O hands down.  Doesn't rely solely on theoretical BS, but uses first hand relevant issues.

Would have dropped the course if it wasn't for the TA
