reviews.comment: Posts all his powerpoints online; however they do not have much info on them and you have to read the course note package he uploads. Lecture are boring since he drones and will spend 30 mins talking about hamburgers or something. Midterm was fair but study way ahead of time cause there's lots of content to learn

The class is all about memorization. In 3 hour lectures he always lets you leave at least 30 minutes early. Posts all presentations and gives out a very detailed note package which covers everything that will be on the exams. Can be dry at some times though.

I did not enjoy his class. It was a very difficult class and he made it even harder by it being so dry. He did not seem knowledgeable about many of the topics we learned and droned on about unimportant things forever. His exams were really hard.

Professor Yan is a great prof and I really enjoyed taking this course with him. His lectures are easy to follow but this course is difficult in that it is all memorization- way more than any ANP class, in my opinion. Take your time memorizing the material- his exams are multiple choice AND short answer so watch out for spelling as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: No textbook, thank God! (I've spent enough on textbooks already!); he posted all his slides/notes on blackboard before the semester even began! :) I was dreading this class, but it was actually really fascinating! There's a TON of material but it's not hard to understand; lots of memorisation. Prof. Yan is a nice guy, exams are very fair.

Interesting and knowledgeable prof! He is super passionate about the topics he teaches and especially C. botulinum!  This is a pure memory course, so if you take the time to memorize the free online text he provides, you will do well.
Great prof definitely a lot of material but clear with expectations and midterms are more than fair if you study adequately. Put in the work and an easy A for sure.

Made a very boring subject surprisingly interesting. Good prof for this course, however if you want a good mark you have to spend a lot of time studying. All the material is presented on his slides and in lectures but requires a lot of memorization.

He was OK. The material was interesting but he just went through everything so slowly I found it hard to concentrate. It definitely didn't help that it was a night class. Lots of memorizing and its easy to get confused between the different pathogens so make sure to practice with cue cards.
Great professor! He was pretty clear on what would be on the midtermsfinal. Listen to what he says in class but don't forget to use the course pack as your guide. Easy A+ if you study
Prof. Yan is da bomb! Take this class with him and you won't be disappointed :)

Dr. Yan is the best prof I have had at UOttawa! He has interesting stories that help with memorizing the MO's for the exams. Its basically pure memory work. The 2 midterms and final are fair. I studied hard for all of them and came out feeling like I overstudied. He is great at answering emails. I loved how there was no textbook just the coursepack

If you can take HSS1100 with this prof, it would be in your BEST interest. First of all, I didn't have to buy a textbook -- he gives you a free course pack on Blackboard with everything you need to know. I printed that at Staples for like, $30. If you read/study it and go to class... easy A.  Super interesting lecturer and responds to emails FAST.
Great and down-to-earth prof. But exams are insanely tough, need to study a week prior to them. Interesting course overall but lots of useless information.
No textbook was needed, but the notes he provided. Nice professor, but sometimes confusing.
Great professor, passionate about his field. Material is easy to grasp if you have a really good memory.
he's very enthusiastic! study the notes and you'll get good grades
Too much information to memorize and his exams are really hard.  He is difficult to understand.  Avoid him if you can.  Needs to use a microphone to be heard.

READ THE COURSE NOTES AND YOU WILL GET AN A+!! Very enthusiastic prof! Makes 3 hour lectures a breeze! Make sure to attend his exam reviews! They are really helpful, he uses stuffed animals and it makes it really memorable and easy to remember which MO belongs to what symptom and such. Wonderful prof!

Great prof. Favourite class this semester. very easy to listen to for 3 hours and makes it interesting. he will add stories to certain kinds of microorganisms so if he says a certain food write it beside the bacteria name! midterm's are fair and can be really easy if you take the time to memorize in advance!

CUTEST ASIAN PROFESSOR EVER. Funny, interesting stories, talks slow enough for you to take notes, midterms are easy if you study. CUTE. Keeps you interested for three hours. LOVE HIMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMM. FAVOURITE PROF OF THE SEMESTER.
An excellent professor. If you study you will do well in this class. No tricks.
A fantastic professor. For the midterms and exams, know the course notes he provides and you will do well.

Liked him as a prof - print out his course notes (not slides!) before you go to class and you won't even have to take your own (except to add stuff that isn't directly in them).  Loved that he had guest lecturers in to talk about topics he was less familiar with, their expertise was really interesting to listen to.

Great Prof, easy to listen to for 3 hours. MUST study, or else this class will be hard for you. To get an A+: attend all classes, memorize organisms' names + general characteristics, listen to his stories and take down key notes (ex: if he tells a story about rice, just write RICE next to the bacteria's name, and you'l be able to answer on an exam)
He knows his stuff and teaches it well. I can't stand when professors read directly from the slides, HE DOESN'T. Hooray!

No textbook, but he provides a whole notebook worth of notes from which he teaches off slides, and might relate topics to his own experiences or other national or global health related events. It's as simple as this, as long as you're good at memorizing you'll do well. Otherwise good luck.
Very good professor. The exams are fair as long as you keep up with material. Useful stories and a funny guy. He is also very knowledgeable.

I did not like him. Gives you way too much information that is not even useful. How the laboratory information can be helpful for nurses???? Extremely hard exams. You have to memorize 40-50 pages for exam. In his notes there are mistakes. He uses medical terminology that is not explained. Avoid this prof and your life will be much easier!!!

Very good prof. he has good stories to help you remember info. he explains things very well. the course pack is easy to study from. exams are tough! you really have to know your stuff. but the content is interesting. he always lets you out early. has guest speakers to mix it up. he is very easy to listen to. i can pay attention for the full 3hrs

course is not hard but not easy. If you keep up with his pace in every lecture, you would be fine on this course. Make sure practice more if you are free, otherwise you will easily lose some marks on test or exam. Anyway, his test and exam are overall pretty fair.
Can't really say much other than he is a great professor. Takes time to explain difficult concepts and it's easy to follow his pace.

Every time I showed up in class, I left more confused than if I learnt it by myself. Think of the most convoluted and messed up way to explain something and that is what he would choose. The exam was much harder compared to what he taught in class, so study the hardest questions that he gives you because that'll be on the exam.
nothing
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Very smart guy, after reading some of his past reviews I was nervous but he is very clear with his notes and goes over how to solve the harder problems in class and gives similar ones on quizzes, which offer room for improvement. But I recommend the text book problems as they give some more in depth questions. Overall pretty chill dude.

for me, his way of explaining things in class is very clear, but trying to follow the class using only his notes wouldnt be advised. our final was MUCH harder than the tests, but doable and graded on a curve. his accent isn't hard to understand at all. he's always smiling in class, but i found him somewhat unapproachable

He was very difficult to understand although he does try hard to speak English. The main problem was that he would only do examples and not explain himself. He was also poor at answering our questions as he never acknowledged them. Overall, he is very knowledgeable but you really have to put the work in. The class is pass/fail with weekly quizzes.
Hard to understand, notes are bad. tests are difficult
Tough final exam. Not a suggestion to take this professor course if you wanna pass.

He has all his notes combined into a 120 page PDF that he uploads at the beginning of the year. He marks it up every so often using Microsoft one note. His writing on his tablet is very poor. Labs serve no purpose. He also can't explain things and is nearly impossible to understand. easy course, learn it via YouTube.

Such a nice guy. His notes are really straight forward. There can be times where it can be easy to get lost during class, but just read over his notes and it'll become clear. I mainly studied off of his notes and did really well on his exams. He made the exams very similar to his notes.

I'll give him credit where it's due! He smiles a lot and his lectures can sometimes be a joy to attend. Other times, it can suck. That's the terrible part: it's inconsistent! His tests were easy for me, but his final exam was terrible at best! His explanations don't help and can, more often than not, lead to more confusion. He's condescends too. :(
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Not accommodating at all, and is not clear while teaching lectures. His tests were pretty easy, but the final was terrible and all MC, leaving no room for part marks. As someone who has taken this class before, its safe to say his final was hard and filled with questions never taught. Also, he provides no practice for the final or study guide.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Took calculus 3 with him. In total, showed a total of 3 times during the entire semester. 2 times for the midterm and 1 time for the final. Study through youtube with professor leonard and solve Xinhou's practice midterm. Easy exams with easy A+
He is the best math teacher I have taken His exams come from given material, and he can explain questions well after class I trust I will take his course again

If you have the option to choose him or someone else, choose the other prof. I went to every class, and if anyone had a question about his example, he would be very condescending when answering and would't give a straight answer. He also failed to adequately prepare the class for the final exam, as his "review" was him saying "study everything"

He is an okay prof. He would've gotten a higher rating. But his tests aren't the greatest. There are a lot of questions where either you're correct or wrong and there's no scope for part marks. That being said he's a good prof. He knows his stuff and he expects you to know your stuff. So I don't find him that hard to follow and he jokes around too
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Cannot understand most things he says.

Very difficult to understand. Often explains concepts in unintuitive ways that will leave you more confused than when you started. When you ask questions he gives an answer but doesn't explain how or why. I highly recommend switching to another section if you have Hua.
really easy if you attend all the lectures and pay attention. Easiest prof available for this course
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Eric is a good prof with great notes for the class, however his exam marking scheme is insane, either its right or wrong. He is barley gives any part marks, where part marks are deserved. He would be rated higher for me if he was more fair with his marking style.

Professor Hua is good mainly because he uses the projector and chalkboard instead of just using the whiteboard/chalkboard. He explains and posts all of his notes online but is sometimes hard to follow. It is not because of his accent mind you, it is because he will expect you to draw lines between steps that you may not understand completely.
no textbook needed cuz he gives specific notes to read and there's plenty of examples that are similar as the questions in the exams

Prof. Hua is pretty standard for a math teacher. He does plenty of examples and will further explain them if asked. While he does have an Asian accent, it is easy to get used to. His tests are the easiest but the exam was brutal. The marking scheme is also great as it includes best 3 of 5 tests and even attendance marks.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Sometimes hard to understand what he is trying to say but makes sense most of the time. Final exam gave me PTSD flashbacks of PHYS 1004 though. Really easy class otherwise. Know your theorems for the final exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Great guy, always happy and his tests are fair and very close to the tutorials he gives you.  Easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Hard to understand

Lectures were useless as you never knew when he stopped teaching theory and started on examples; I only did good was because I just did past test/exams to study. The notes he post are great alternative to the textbook, save your money.

Eric Hua is like most profs for math at Carleton. Most likely you will not be able to understand him with his asian accent. Bless him, he does try to teach the material. Read the textbook! You will understand all the concepts if you take the time to read the book, and do some of the problems. Exam was multiple choice, and similar to previous years
long and boring lecture.  It's hard to concentrate on his lecture, since the speaking speed..  avoid him if possible.

Good prof in general, very friendly and always smiling.  Assignments and midterms were  easy, but he screws you over with the final.  The jump in difficulty from the midterms to the final was HUGE.  Even if you are doing well in this course, study hard for the final, you're going to need it.
He is a good prof, fairly clear

Awesome prof. He does have a slight Chinese accent but it doesn't hinder his teaching. He does the math problems nicely, and will explain further when requested. The greatest thing is that the questions he puts on the tests is in the exact same style as the questions he does in class, normally even easier. He always smiles too, which is a bonus.

Dr. Hua is about the happiest guy I've ever had at the front of any class, which I personally feel makes a large difference. On top of that, he conveyed the content well, he was always excellently organised for class, and he always responded informatively to questions. I couldn't ask more of any professor.
He's nice and good at teaching. Organized and clear lectures. He makes everything easy! Chinese accent but speaks very clearly:) Review the notes, easy to get good mark!
A good instructor, notes are clear.

Very easy course with this professor. Notes are available on CULearn, as are tutorials with solutions! Quizzes are easy, as was the final, only catch is that the final is MCQ. Zero classes attended, easy A, enough said.

Although I really enjoyed his lectures, my opinion on him changed greatly after the exam. I went to see my exam and he told me how terribly I did on it as well as I need a tutor in front of a group of people, which was quite humiliating. He also was not prepared to answer any questions regarding the mistakes we made on the exam.
Nice and easy. Just prep for the exam..because if he didnt make it.. its gonna be slightly harder

His tests are all very easy compared to the other profs. final exams were hard for us relative to first year math courses but this man probably bell curved the marks so we all get the mark we wanted. great prof besides the chinese accent (well that's his character)
Great Prof he always does helpful exmaples on the board. He's also always happy.

Really hard time understanding his thick Chinese accent, but did get used to it. He pulls his test questions directly from examples (example, huh?!) in class, and tutorials. Easy prof but you have to learn the material on your own.
One of the better math profs at CU. Smart guy and an excellent character. One of those people in life that you can't not like.

this guy is a straight beauty.  Go to his lectures take down his examples if anything, use the homework questions he posts on webct to study from his tests and there will be no suprises whatsoever.Dope Proff, always smiling
Best math prof. Doesn't show off  by mentioning his experience and achievements. He shows that by the way he teaches and his proficiency of the course's knowledge.

Really great guy, knows a lot about calculus and is very patient with students. Attend his lectures, and you'll do fine. He doesn't use the book AT ALL though. You won't regret picking him; he always has a smile on his face!

Wow! Great prof, very humorous. He is easy to understand, his notes are wonderful and he teaches with a great big smile. He is hard to understand at first because of his geographical accent but after a few weeks you end up pronouncing everything like him and it's all good.

The best math prof. Kind of tough to understand at first. A surprisingly good sense of humor. Makes great use of webct. Good teacher. Pay attention to all his examples- these will be your exam questions.
Best math prof in carleton!! Attend his class you will not regret it!
His class was great and the tests were really easy! Not hard to get 100%. The exam was way harder then the tests though. Over all a good teacher and his notes online are amazing!

Im an older student who switched programs so Ive experienced an array of profs in business and law. Xinhou is a nice guy.The course is structured fairly and he marks fairly as well.My issue is with his clarity.He has a very strong accent which is hard to understand. Lectures are very boring (it's math). Learned solely from my textbook.
OMG if you can read what he puts on the board your good to go. I didn't realize how much I like him untill I had other profs.
quiz and test are easy. read all his tutorial notes you will be ok in the final although it is a bit hard than usual

Funny prof, hard to understand at the beginning of each class, but does get easier throughout the class.  Tests are challenging especially since they are only out of 15, so if you get a mark off you lose a lot. Can be unclear on certain things, but check the textbook, his notes come from there.
Strong accent, hard to follow at first. Content in the beginning is rather dry but it picks up. Definitely get the study guide that goes with the text book.
Best math prof ever had him earlier for 1104 and i got used to his accent there.  As a prof he helps alot just by doing examples in class he makes up as he goes.  Complete math genius.

He was my prof for MATH 1101 too.. he is a great prof. he will have every single one of his notes available to you. his online notes are self explaining. he is a good prof to take if you are not so good in math. his test and exams are the EASIEST.

I stopped attending class. All notes are online but in class he slowly repeats them which some how made me MORE CONFUSED with all the YINCONSISTENT WARIABLE WECTOR WEE! The final was WAY harder than the tests. Didn't help that my ta had a twitch & answered every question with OBVIOUSLY & nothing else! Sorry comp sci's you can't escape the WECTORS!!

Seems to know his stuff but his accent is to thick it's hard to understand him. Laughs like an evil genius if someone asks a question that's too simple. Amusing to watch, but lectures weren't helpful to me.
This prof is doing a great job in this class, honestly, he explains well. I recommend him for you guys...
Might of failed , but i think he was a good prof in the long run :P Just the tests are pretty much the tutorials again.
Awesome! Smartest prof. I've ever seen. I've had him in 3 different classes now, and I love having him as my prof. Takes a little used to his accent though, but he's not that bad.
best prof...

I did not like him! His English is totally not understandable. I attended someone elses lecture for the course. Although this course is very easy but due is way of teaching I had to work very hard. I would advise you to not take his lectures!

This guys is a complete absolute GENIUS... all examples he made them up as he went. Easy test, clear notes and the most amusing guy ever... he laughs for no reason. BUT his accent is pretty ahrd to understand... slope = sloop, wii = v, lektive = negative, and he always says "this is IMPORTANT!!!"... funiest and smartest guy. great PROF.

This is my favorite so far. Notes are esay to understand. Course is pretty easy to follow. I love this guy! He has a funny accent tho, like the "inwos" means the "inverse", "slope of a nine" for "slope of a line". I still love him tho!
the best math teacher ever, makes difficult courses easy, nice man
Good Prof! Tests were pretty difficult but overall a pretty good guy. Accent is fairly amusing. Par exemple, "wii"locity, asym"totas", sloop of a line, etc. Good course

Really good prof and easy marker. He's kind of hard to understand with his accent, but he explains everything really well and he doesn't write much junk on the board so you can write his notes and then listen to him explain it. I would take a class with this prof again if possible.

I had this professor for linear algebra (MAT1341). Although its hard to understand his lectures as he goes too fast and has a thick accent, the midterms were fair. If you are looking to self learn he is the professor, but overall a nice and respectful professor.

very kind guy. good sense of humour and interesting course material. one of, if not the best professor I've had. Gem of uOttawa. I wish him well. (this is for MAT1341 but I cant seem to add that code)
approachable and very clean and precise lecture notes.

Prof is very good, caring, make sure you understands the materials. He always have extra office hours where he supported anyone with questions. Although, you should studied on your own, coming basically new to calculus and just going to his lectures are not going to be enough because his teaching are fast. Exams are super fair. Great prof.
Great professor with a great attitude towards students. Would highly recommend him to anyone planning to take their Calculus pre-requisite.

My favorite teacher so far, she really cares for her students. She shows concern where it's needed, and explains things clearly. She takes things rather quickly, but if you even pay attention for only 70% of the time, her simple and easy-to-keep-up teaching methods will help a lot. 9 times out of 10 the slide decks she posts are enough.

10/10

HATE. THIS. CLASS. I loved learning Japanese before this class but now I'm planning on giving up..She puts us into small pairs and we have to do homework on the spot on zoom in groups of four random classmates...its so stressful and awkward if you get the answer wrong..she also assigns us a lot of homework to do outside of class as well as in class
Aizu sensei is so sweet. Her classes were so much fun. Even though it was bi-modal, she did her best to help all of the students. I really enjoyed her classes. She's also an easy grader.

Yoriko is an excellent prof, she's also very nice and helpful. Though there were tasks to submit for each class which made the course a bit heavy, they weren't too difficult and are a good way to practice a language in my opinion. Tests and assignments are fairly reasonable and she's not a tough grader, especially for speaking/oral tests.
Yoriko is so nice and easy on the grade compared to other Japanese teachers. Hell I'd take Yoriko any day. I'd take the class because its Yoriko!!!!!

She is a very good prof and very nice. Provides inline feedback on homework.
However, do expect lots of homework. It is very homework heavy and fast but she is the opposite of a tough grader, especially for speaking/reading tests. As long as you spend the time doing the homework (like a math course), you will get a good grade.
Great prof who provides excellent feedback! Would def take again (and am)

As a entry level language teacher, Yoriko Aizu definitely did a good job leading student into the new language. She is very patient, helpful and easy to reach out, give fast feedbacks on all works. However the I find her as a touch marker, one small mistake and gets full mark taken away on homework.

Yoriko-sensei is a delightful prof and a lovely human being. She was willing to schedule one-on-one sessions if we were struggling with anything and she explained things really well and in depth. The assignments were all reflective of what we were learning and really helped with understanding the content. The tests were reasonably challenging.

Aizu sensee was really charismatic even through Zoom lectures. Her homeworks and tests were fair but I found the final to be a bit long. If you attend class, participate and practice you'll do fine. Would take again!
Legendary

Aizu Sensei was the best professor I've had in all my years of studying at University. She is very caring and considerate when grading. Her enthusiasm when teaching is nothing to be taken for granted. To do well, show up, listen, and practice at home. Nothing else to it, she is very fair with her evaluations.

Professor Aizu was very understanding and cheerful. She did call on students to answer, but if they didn't know the answer, she didn't push. She was so kind and had a great sense of humour. She knows how to teach in a way that makes learning Japanese much less intimidating than what it could be. I would definitely recommend taking a class with her!
She is good and patient. The class is an intensive class compared to other foreign language class. Do not think you can get a A without putting so much effort in it.
very nice and lovely, always smile and very patient to answer all the questions you have.
very nice person.

Yoriko-sensei was one of the better professors I've ever had. She made learning Japanese easier than I thought. Usually available if you had questions and the lectures were  interesting and interactive. Class was rarely boring! Has a lot of easy assignmentsquizzes so if you study it's easy to follow your progress as the semester happens.

She was a very good prof, always prepared. Lots of assignments, but they were all very easy. She calls on people in class, so study. The tests are exactly the same information that you learn in class. She knows how to teach so that learning Japanese wasn't hard. You must use your textbook in class. She was also always nice and positive. Good vibes.
Take this class if you are interested in Japanese, it's great!

Yoriko-sensei is patient, friendly and great professor of JPN1901! Highly recommended Go to her office in office hours, she will help you. Put effort and have time to practice for learning Japanese and for her quizzes. It's not easy to learn a new language but be patient, it will take time. You will get the hang of Japanese language soon.

Yoriko-sensei is such a sweetheart! Her class was the most enjoyable one during my semester. She always posted the powerpoints of the week before. Lots of quizzes and assignments, but that's normal for a language class. She's a bit harsher than other profs when it comes to correction for orals but it's possible to get a 100% on mid-terms and finals
Best teacher ever! She's a sweetheart and always willing to help you! :) Of course you'll have a lot of work to do, but that's normal since you're learning a new language.
Great class, not always super clear but if you talk and ask questions, she is very helpful and super nice!

I completed this class last semester and I honestly still miss it to this day. It was a great, fun, and rewarding class to attend. Yoriko-sensei was a sweetheart and you always felt comfortable asking anything. Work load is heavy but that is normal for a language course! Thank you for everything Yoriko-Sensei for one of the best courses I've taken!
Simply loved her! Powerpoints are well organized and easy to follow, encourages participation and makes good use of the book. Passed with an A
Great sensei!! She is very nice and patient to all students. Easy to understand, well organized, very helpful for leaarning Japanese!! Take her class!!
Really great sensei! The only thing was that the JPN 1902 course covers so much material, it's very hard remembering everything.Would be fun to have some field trips to practice all together.
Very enthusiastic, extremely kind and always willing to help. Makes sure that the class understands concepts before moving on. Fabulous professor.

Adorable in a way that only the Japanese can achieve. She is  a good teacher with lets you know what she is expecting from you from the get go. Just be ready to speak a language you are just starting to learn if you do something she doesn't like, cause she calls on the people who don't pay attention
Very excellent prof! Easy to understand, and goes out of her way to help if you're confused!! Quick to respond to emails. Came out of the course with an A+.

Want to hate math? Take his class, does basically no examples & says its "easy math". He's lecture heavy and his lectures don't help at all. He is all over the place and isn't organized, goes from topic to topic and doesn't explain. Confused? He'll say go look at the book. Only good thing is he gives study guides for tests NOT quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I selected extra credit but not really, he just gives lots of partial credit on tests. Class was terrible, someone cried in class and he just kept going. Don't know of many people that passed this semester. I'd wait for another professor before taking him again. He laughed at our grades. Class avg was 40, highest 80 on first test. Got worse.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He gives practice problems that are VERY similar to the tests. VERY lecture heavy. Many people dropped the class. Several people cried during class. I put "extra credit" but it isn't really "extra." He is very generous with partial credit on the tests. He talks fast, writes faster. Don't blink, you'll miss an example problem. ONLY TWO TESTS.
Proceeded to smile while announcing the class average(30) then blames us because of it. Doesn't really explain the math just expects everyone to know already.

Is satisfied with students failing. Does not explain work clearly and lowkey tries to belittle you during class for not knowing “simple” math. I wouldn't dare recommend him to anyone. He smiled while announcing the class average(which was a 30)like he enjoyed that it was that low. If you don't already know Cal II, don't expect to learn it from him.
Second test class average was 30 yeah it's 2nd review. Whole class failing he says it's our problem.
Class is difficult, test 1 average was 40. Calc 2 isn't optional so gotta take it again :(

Dr. Chen was an amazing professor. Yes, his accent makes him a bit harder to understand however the lectures were very thorough. Homework is given just about every week and it is very helpful! Before a test he gives out a very useful study guide that is very similar to the test and he goes through it and works out each problem.

I took this over the summer, and I made an A. I was failing when I took it at Auburn Uni. The practice problems help, and the study guides are very similar to the tests. I 1000% recommend you take this class. He has a thick accent, but his notes are legible and easy to understand. Midterm 30%, Final 40%, take home quizzes 30%, attendance 5% bonus

Took him in the summer. Write everything he writes on the board. He gives partial credit if you had the right process just messed up the numbers. Study guides very similar to test test, STUDY THEM! He was a great teacher, would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed Dr. Chen's class. Very organized and clear grading.

Had him for Pre cal and Finite. I often found it difficult to understand him during lectures. I'd have to search through the textbooks and get tutored in order to make the subject and topics much clearer. Study guides are very similar to exams.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I took professor Yue Chen class online for Finite Math, and it wasn't as tough as I thought this class would be. He gives you quizzes for each section of a chapter and you have 3 tries and the highest attempt is keep for your grade. You must meet your deadline because this is no make up work. I made a 92 in this class.

Calc 2 is not the easiest math class to take, but Dr. Chen does a really good job. He is the best instructor I have had in math.  All the calc classes give a lot of HW, but he doesnt collect it. He gives quizzes that cover what he wants you to know for the test. His test reviews are pretty good as well.   He is fair and he cares. TAKE HIS CLASS

By far the best MATH professor I've ever had. I have taken his classes from pre-cal thru cal 2. He is thorough in explaining concepts and is always willing to help if your understanding is lacking. The notes he gives in class are helpful, organized, and clear. Doing the HW assignments is a MUST. He gives a weekly quiz on material from previous week
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Expect homework out of each section you cover and weekly quizzes directly from the homework. If you do the homework you'll do fine on the quizzes. He gives review problems for the test, do those and you'll be fine on the test. He also gives extra credit worksheets. DO THEM. He adds them to your final grade. Also, the final is hard.. So study a lot!
If you ever get the chance to take a class given by this professor do so

The professor is one of a kind,  absolutely amazing!!!!!!! I took the class as an elective, and I enjoyed it more than I could expect to enjoy a class. They are Understanding towards students, make it very possible and easy for everyone to get A's while learning, take it you will not regret this, you'll enjoy it and still get a+grades, no stress.
Wow! This professor is a God sent. So caring about his student's mental health and tests are so easy as he does an excellent job at teaching the material. I 100000% reccomend him!!

Unfortunately, this teacher is seriously outdated on technology and research methods. This course was totally disappointing and useless. Poorly prepared, no slides, only long mostly off-topic monologues lasting over 3 hours every class. Harsh grader. Unless you want your GPA to drop, stay away.

Professor Laberge is one of a kind. He focused on critical thinking over memorization, making the material engaging and personal. He took the time to carefully review each exam and paper, providing constructive comments. His detailed feedback on exams and papers helped me improve and boosted my confidence, inspiring me to pursue my master's degree.

This teacher is friendly but kept contradicting himself about how to approach the exams and how they would be evaluated. He did not know how to teach the course effectively, nor was he organized or objective in his evaluations, as no grading criteria were provided or clarified. Some students failed because of it. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: (Elective) I was pleasantly surprised with how much I enjoyed it. The professor is very passionate and values open conversation with the students during class rather than reading off PowerPoint slides. Open-book exams and no info regurgitating required! Makes you think on practical applications of concepts. Would totally take a class with him again

Prof. Laberge is clearly very passionate about the material. No powerpoints or notes provided, but lectures were all recorded on Zoom. His teaching method is not for everyone, as he dives very deep into some topics. One midterm (50%) and a final (50%) with relatively easy questions. He was always happy to provide extra help and feedback.

Professor is very knowledgeable, but humble.  The content of the course was relevant and he was always concerned about supporting our learning and comprehension.  Professor Laberge was able to explain complex concepts in a way that was accessible.  Understanding the concepts was more important than pushing content.  Very caring.

Mr. Yves Laberge excels in teaching, brilliantly combining passion and expertise. Dedicated and approachable, he creates a stimulating classroom atmosphere, conducive to learning. His clear and innovative methodology makes concepts understandable and engaging.

I had Professor Laberge for an education class, PED 4803 (not EDU5463), and he was great. He is extremely knowledgeable and couldn't be trumped by any difficult questions, which meant the class could go as in-detail as our interest called for. A great listener, he made himself available and clearly cared about his students. I highly recommend him.

I actually really liked him! His class is all writing based which was a refresher from all mcq. There's a ton of readings but it was doable if you read each paper for roughly an hour and take notes on them. He provides good insight on readings. All assessments are open book. We had 2 midterms worth 30% each with 3 questions and a take home final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Laberge extended my boundaries of critical thought in his pedagogy, through texts and lectures that were specifically relevant and essential to a healthy, well-rounded, 3rd year seminar in Religious Studies. He was very helpful. His assignments and evaluations were rigorous if you wanted to snag a higher grade, but also anticipative.

J'aimerais mettre de l'avant la qualité de l'enseignement de Monsieur Laberge. En plus d'être extrêmement sympathique, M Laberge est aussi un passionné, et ça se ressent quand il enseigne. Son enseignement m'a donné envie d'approfondir mes connaissances. De plus, il arrive a amené le groupe a échangé, et cela rend le cours dynamique. Je recommande.

J'ai eu Pr. Laberge deux fois pendant mon cursus universitaire, et c'est l'un des professeurs des plus marquants! Nous avons étudié plusieurs corpus de textes diversifiés, qui ont grandement amélioré ma culture générale, compétence à l'écrit et mon esprit critique,. Il n'hésite pas à aller à la rencontre des étudiants pour assurer notre réussite!

Professeur Laberge, est l'un des professeur qui m'a inspiré durant ma dernière année de bacalauréat de part sa méthode d'enseignement. Il a su captiver notre attention, même si les cours étaient offert en ligne. Ces exposés magistraux, ces lectures dirigées, nos discussions hedomadaires et aussi mes recherches individuelles m'ont assuré un A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Laberge is amazing! He responds to students' emails soon every time, and he also cares about his students. His lectures were interesting, but there is a lot to learn. I would like to take his course again.

Taking Professor Laberge's course was one of the best decisions in my life. He is a kind, wise, and broad-thinking person. As a professor, he really wants his students to succeed and always brings a lot of useful feedback to his students. Besides, his grading is quite fair; hence, I could get a good mark in his class. Best prof at uOttawa!

Best teacher I have ever had. Dr. Laberge helped me so much, and gave amazing lectures. I learned a lot from him. He is very kind, and caring for his students. He goes above and beyond to help his students. Wish all teachers were like him. Truly a gem, and an passionate intellect! He should teach more classes, would definitely take him again!

His style of teaching and lecturing is what truly sets him apart from other professors in the faculty of social sciences. He promoted a hybrid teaching platform where he lectured live but also recorded the lectures for future viewing. He would greatly concern himself with his students' progress and build rapport with his student body (inclusive)

Amazing prof! Would take any chance to have him as a prof again! Honestly he is a real gem as he is super accessibly outside of class. He is willing to go above and beyond to help students! Really wish he taught more courses! Don't hesitate and take him as a prof!

Prof. Laberge is very passionate about the issues he teaches about. He is extremtly knowledgeable and explains the material in a simple way. He is a joy to be around and his tests are very straight forward. Go to class take notes and youll do fine. Would suggest.

Great professor. Very involved in and outside of class and really knows the material. Lecture heavy but he makes sure all students understand the content before moving on. Very helpful and you can tell he wants his students to do well.

Dr. Laberge was the greatest professor I have had since going to uOttawa! I was a first-year student who passed with flying colours, so what does that tell you? Dr. Laberge truly cares about his students, knows his criteria, and does everything he can to help his students' success!

Super nice guy, just not the best lecturer. His 3h lectures could've easily been 1.5h tops. He is super knowledgeable though and truly cares about his students, he just doesn't always know how to get the info across and rambles on a lot. Overall, a decent prof

Dr. Laberge is a great professor who truly cares about his students! The course content offers critical insight on several state actors and geo-political human rights issues. Extra research outside of the course material may be required to get over an 80% on exams. However, all the material necessary to pass the course is available for students.

I had an amazing experience with this class and this prof. I love this material and Prof. Laberge broke down the material in a way that was easy to understand and always answered questions in class or in a quick and timely manner outside of class. He provided multiple reading that helped with the midterms and exams. Overall really good experience!
Great prof, truly cares about his students. Can't think of any criticism about him.

Was incredibly caring and the content of the syllabus was fantastic. Prof will take time to make the class accessible for everyone and give amazing lectures. The exams are solid if you're prepared for them, just make sure you do the readings!!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Phenomenal professor. One of the best classes Ive taken. Genuinely cares for students, and takes the time to explain and help.

Hands down one of the best professors at uOttawa. He devotes his time to ensure his students understand the material (Readings, lectures,videos). His passion for Human Rights shines through his teaching and it makes students stay engaged and show up for the lectures. I would most definitely take his class again because I learnt a ton in his class.

The absolute kindest professor you will ever meet. It is so clear that he cares about his students and is passionate about teaching. Our class loved him and he never failed to put a smile on our faces!

Professor Laberge is a real gem. He is the best prof I will ever have in uOttawa. He is kind and persistent and understanding. He gives you real knowledge . he makes you learn through all odd's . He is a definition of what a prof should be doing in uOttawa. I will never regret this class in my life. He has opened my eyes in human rights so so much.

Easily one of my favorite professor's, if not my favorite. He really cares about his students! I enjoy his lectures, he's passionate about his career and interests and makes it easy to succeed. No textbook (not for ECH 2300 either), just some decent readings and some short youtube videos. If you put in the work, you will be rewarded!

Yves Laberge became one of my favorite professors. He is so caring about his students and always tries to make time for them. He is not a tough grader; however, I'll suggest reading what he posts on Brightspace to get a good mark. He does not have a heavy Quebecois accent so you won't have any issues understanding his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Readings & videos are very relevant to what was discussed in seminar and what was tested. He prefers essay style questions (gives a bank of questions and expects students to answer at least two in 2-3 pages). He takes the time to meet outside of class via zoom to give feedback (his feedback is very helpful). I learned a lot in this class.

yves Laberge est le prof le plus cute et attentionné que j'ai connue dans toute ma vie. Contrairement aux autres profs il s'intéresent grandement aux élèves et fait tout pour nous. Il est toujours disponible et crée une bonne relation avec les élèves. il est très sociable et très easy going. le meilleur prof. je l'adore.

I am so glad and impressed to have Dr. Laberge's class at my last year in the U of Ottawa. He is one of the best professors I've met during my college life. He is not an easy marker, but every effort you've made will be rewarded. I definitely want to take more courses with Dr. Laberge if one day I decide to go back to school and continue my study.

one of the best teacher CDN 1500 easy marks to get and for the quizzes and finals, he gives you the questions 1 week before and easy grader. If you definitely want to pass a class, take this course with him.
Super sweet teacher. Really kind and very relaxed/laid back. Very flexible and understanding. I suggest him to anyone who's looking to have a great teacher and good grades for not much work.

I had M. Laberge for all the courses he offers at uOttawa - canadian studies, in cinema, and in international development. He's the most flexible prof I've had, he is constructive and his pedagogy actually helps you understand the different themes in class. He wants student to learn without being harsh or tough.
Her classes are difficult but she is incredibly reflective and thoughtful. Assignment are hard but if you try to engage the material you will learn a lot.

Do not take this class. Zipporah is a horrible Professor. Reads directly from readings all class. Never lets you out on time. Complete arbitrary, and very low marks. Lectures are very boring and unhelpful. Online powerpoints contain no valuable information. Will often spend 30 minutes trying to make you discuss things with the person beside you.

Has no idea what she's talking about. She's appointed to the philosophy department, but it's like she's never taken a philosophy course in her life. If the TAs weren't there we'd have no idea what was going on at all. Very disorganized, technologically illiterate. Pushes her agenda, and doesn't allow for debate.
